title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Description of Cboe Aggregated Market Feed (Cboe One) in Rule 13.8
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Description of Cboe Aggregated Market Feed (Cboe One) in Rule 13.8

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 13.8(b), which currently lists the specific data elements and message types in the Cboe One Feed, to instead identify the sources of the Cboe One Feed: (1) the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 13.8(a) and the Multicast Depth feeds of BZX, BYX, and EDGA (collectively, the ``Multicast Depth Feeds''); and (2) the SIPs. The proposed rule text also states that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. This approach is consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable aggregated market data products by identifying their sources rather than specifying message formats or field-level content, as discussed below. By way of background, the Cboe One Feed is currently offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, each of which contains information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds and from the SIPs. The versions differ only in the quotation information each provides. Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two- sided quotations at multiple price levels, currently up to twelve per side per exchange. Execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information are the same in both versions. The current Cboe One Feed includes the following information from the Multicast Depth Feeds: individual last sale information for the Exchange and each of its affiliated exchanges, as well as Symbol Summary, Market Status, Retail Liquidity Identifier, Trading Status, and Trade Break messages. It also includes the following information from the SIPs: consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price for all listed equity securities. The Cboe One Feed also disseminates the following information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds: the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price. For securities listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the BZX Official Opening Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(5), and the Cboe One Closing Price is the BZX Official Closing Price as defined in BZX Rule 11.23(a)(3). For securities not listed on BZX, the Cboe One Opening Price is the first last sale eligible trade that occurs on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the Cboe One Closing Price is the final last sale eligible trade to occur on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges prior to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The five price level version of Cboe One Premium is scheduled to be sunset no later than December 31, 2026, and the Exchange announced via Exchange Notice that it will be sunset effective November 2, 2026. As of that date, Cboe One Premium will be offered only with up to twelve aggregated price levels per side per exchange, which have been available since May 4, 2026. The Exchange has historically amended Rule 13.8(b) by name each time it added a data element to the Cboe One Feed, even where the new data element fell within a type of information the feed already carried. For example, the Exchange filed a proposed rule change to add the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, obtained directly from the SIPs and disseminated after the applicable SIP delay period, and later filed a separate proposed rule change to add the current day consolidated high and low price, also obtained directly from the SIPs. Each of these filings added a discrete data element obtained from information disseminated by the SIPs, a source already reflected in the feed. The Exchange now proposes to describe the Cboe One Feed by its sources so that the addition of a data element, or a change to an existing data element, obtained from a source identified in Rule 13.8(b) will not require a separate proposed rule change. As proposed, Rule 13.8(b) would provide that the Cboe One Feed contains information obtained from two sources: the Multicast Depth Feeds and the SIPs. It would further provide that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BZX, BYX, and EDGA, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. The proposed rule text would not specify the number of price levels in Cboe One Premium, itemize categories of information, or define ``consolidated market information.'' Those details describe the current content of the feed, as discussed below. The amended rule would define the Cboe One Feed by the sources from which its content is obtained and by the quotation information each version provides, rather than by a list of individual data elements, message names, prices, or price levels. A recipient would continue to subscribe to either Cboe One Summary or Cboe One Premium. The proposed rule text deletes from Rule 13.8(b): (i) the itemized list of data elements, including the references to consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price; (ii) the names of individual messages, including the parenthetical attributing the Retail Liquidity Identifier to BYX; (iii) the Depth of Book subparagraph, including the references to five and twelve price levels and the sunset of the five level feed of Cboe One Premium; and (iv) the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price methodology. In their place, the proposed rule text identifies

raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change by the Options Clearing Corporation Relating to the Addition of the Evergreen Provisions to OCC's LRMF

1. Purpose OCC proposes changes to its LRMF to memorialize the Evergreen Provisions that describe the circumstances in which OCC may renew three liquidity facilities described in detail below without filing an advance notice. Including these Evergreen Provisions will improve the completeness of the LRMF and make it more efficient to track the circumstances in which the facilities may be renewed without an advance notice. Each of the three facilities and the current conditions under which OCC may renew the facility without filing an advance notice are described below. Revolving Credit Facility OCC maintains a revolving credit facility for a 364-day term that it may use: (i) to meet obligations arising out of the default or suspension of a Clearing Member or any action taken by OCC to address such a default or suspension; (ii) to reimburse OCC for bankruptcy losses, subject to the conditions set forth in the By-Laws and Rules; (iii) to the extent permitted by the By-Laws and Rules, (a) to obtain funds projected to be required by OCC in anticipation of a potential default by, or suspension of, a Clearing Member; or (b) to address liquidity needs for daily settlement obligations as the result of the failure of any bank, securities or commodities clearing organization, or investment counterparty to perform any obligation to OCC when due (``Revolving Credit Facility''). The Revolving Credit Facility provides short-term secured borrowings in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion but may be increased to $3.5 billion if OCC so requests and sufficient commitments from lenders are received and accepted. To obtain a loan under the Revolving Credit Facility, OCC would pledge as collateral: (i) U.S. dollars; (ii) securities issued or guaranteed by the U.S. Government or the Government of Canada; (iii) equities included in the S&P 500 Market Index, the NASDAQ exchange, or any United States or Canadian national securities exchange; (iv) Exchange- Traded Funds (``ETFs''); or (v) American Depositary Receipts (``ADRs''). It is renewed annually for a 364-day term. OCC must submit an advance notice prior to renewing the Revolving Credit Facility if it intends to make changes to the commitment period (which would continue to be 364 calendar days unless changes are necessary to avoid the expiration of the term falling on a weekend or other day that is not a business day). However, without submitting an advance notice, OCC may: (1) increase the commitment amounts so long as the increase (whether in the initial commitment amount, additional commitment amount, or both) is by no more than $500 million in total as compared to the 2025 Bank Syndicate Revolving Credit Facility, which authorized a $2.5 billion initial commitment that could be increased to $3.5 billion if OCC so requests and sufficient commitments from lenders are received and accepted; (2) decrease the commitment amounts by up to $500 million so long as any decrease in the initial commitment amount is replaced by other qualifying liquid resources (as defined in Exchange Act Rule 17ad- 22(a)(14) ) of an equal amount; (3) add new lenders or remove existing lenders so long as all lenders to future renewals are subject to the same credit review as those lenders that were party to its 2020 Bank Syndicate Revolving Credit Facility; (4) change the lead administrative agent and/or the backup administrative agent so long as the new agent in future renewals is subject to the requirements for selecting providers of core services set forth OCC's policies and procedures; (5) change pricing and collateral haircuts, so long as such terms are consistent with the then-current market practice; and (6) change other terms and conditions of the agreement so long as the changes do not materially affect the nature or level of risk presented to OCC. Bank Repo Facility OCC also maintains a master repurchase agreement with a bank counterparty as part of its overall liquidity plan (``Bank Repo Facility''). Pursuant to the Bank Repo Facility, the buyer (i.e., the bank counterparty) agrees to purchase from OCC, from time to time, U.S. Government securities. OCC, as the seller, would transfer these securities to the buyer in exchange for a payment by the buyer to OCC in immediately available funds. The buyer would simultaneously agree to transfer the purchased securities back to OCC at a specified later date or on OCC's demand against the transfer of funds by OCC to the buyer in an amount equal to the amount the buyer paid plus the accrued and unpaid price differential, which is the interest component of the agreement. The buyer provides a funding commitment of up to $1 billion, with the commitment extending for one year (plus or minus one day). The Bank Repo Facility is renewed annually. OCC would submit another advance notice with respect to such renewal for the same term only if: (i) OCC determines its liquidity needs merit funding levels above the $1 billion, (ii) OCC should seek to change the terms and conditions of the Master Repurchase Agreement (``MRA'') in a manner that materially affects the nature or level of risk presented by OCC, (iii) OCC should seek to add counterparties or substitute the bank counterparty to the Bank Repo Facility program, or (iv) the bank counterparty has experienced a negative change to its credit profile or a material adverse change since the latest renewal of the MRA. Non-Bank Liquidity Facility OCC also maintains a program for accessing additional committed sources of liquidity that do not increase the concentration of OCC's counterparty exposures (``Non-Bank Liquidity Facility''). The Non-Bank Liquidity Facility is comprised of two parts: an MRA and confirmations with one or more institutional investors, which contain certain individualized terms and conditions of transactions executed between OCC, the institutional investors and their agents. The MRA is structured like a typical repurchase arrangement. This facility has no commitment

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE National, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE National, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend the Connectivity Fee Schedule regarding colocation services and fees to update the list of included data products (``Included Data Products''). Currently, the table of Included Data Products in Colocation Note 4 sets forth the market data feeds that Users can connect to at no additional cost when they purchase a service that includes access to the LCN or IP network. The Exchange proposes to update the table of Included Data Products to include NYSE Options Select, a data feed that consists of a subset of data from the OPRA consolidated data feed that has been curated by the Exchange's Affiliate SRO NYSE. Given the growing number of options series and the increasing popularity of options trading, the OPRA consolidated data feed is voluminous and requires market participants to dedicate significant amounts of bandwidth to receive it. The NYSE Options Select data feed would provide market participants the ability to view critical NBBO, trade data, and administrative messages from the OPRA data feed without consuming the full OPRA data set, thereby decreasing bandwidth requirements and costs when compared to the full OPRA data feed. Other exchange groups currently offer similar selections of the OPRA data feed, including the Nasdaq Smart Options and Cboe Options Lite data feeds. To implement the change, the Exchange proposes to update the table of Included Data Products as follows (proposed addition italicized): NYSE Bonds. NYSE Options Select. NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO. NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO Snapshot. NYSE Texas. NYSE Texas Aggregated Lite. NYSE Texas BBO. NYSE Texas Integrated Feed. NYSE Texas Order Imbalances. NYSE Texas Trades. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ As indicated, the Exchange plans to offer connectivity to two different NYSE Options Select data feeds: NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO, which includes real-time trades and real-time NBBO updates for all OPRA symbols, and NYSE Options Select Trades & NBBO Snapshot, which includes real-time trades for all OPRA symbols plus an NBBO snapshot at the time of a trade (collectively the ``NYSE Options Select data feeds''). The Exchange does not charge for connectivity to the Included Data Feeds. Accordingly, it would not charge for connectivity to the NYSE Options Select data feeds. Application and Impact of the Proposed Changes The proposed rule change would not apply differently to distinct types or sizes of market participants. Rather, it would apply to all Users equally. As is currently the case, the purchase of any colocation service is completely voluntary and the Connectivity Fee Schedule is applied uniformly to all Users. The proposed change is not otherwise intended to address any other issues relating to colocation services or related fees, and the Exchange is not aware of any problems that Users would have in complying with the proposed change. Implementation The proposed rule change will become operational when the NYSE Options Select data feeds are available. The Exchange will announce the date through a customer notice. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, because it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest and because it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange further believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act, because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities. The Proposed Rule Change Is Reasonable The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is reasonable and would perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, because adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds would increase the number of Included Data Products available to Users for no additional charge. All Users that voluntarily select to access the LCN or IP network would not be subject to a charge above and beyond the fee paid for the relevant LCN or IP network access. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed change is reasonable because the change would mean that a User would have the option of adding connectivity to additional market data feeds without paying additional charges. Adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds to the list of Included Data Products would allow a User to connect to the NYSE Options Select data feeds if it wished but would not require it to do so. As currently, a User would be able to determine which Included Data Products, if any, to which it connects, based on what would best serve its needs, tailoring the service to the requirements of its business operations. By adding the NYSE Options Select data feeds, the proposed change would ensure that the list of Included Data Products was up to date. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is reasonable and would perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, as it would ensure that the description of Included Data Products was complete, ensuring that it is accessible and transparent, and providing market participants with clarity as to what connectivity is included in th

Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.22(j), which currently lists the specific data elements and message types in the Cboe One Feed, to instead identify the sources of the Cboe One Feed: (1) the Multicast Depth feed of the Exchange described in Rule 11.22(c) and the Multicast Depth feeds of BYX, EDGA, and EDGX (collectively, the ``Multicast Depth Feeds''); and (2) the SIPs. The proposed rule text also states that the Cboe One Feed is offered in two versions, which differ in the quotation information each provides: Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders on the Exchange, BYX, EDGA, and EDGX, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two-sided quotations for displayed orders on each such exchange at multiple price levels. This approach is consistent with the manner in which other exchange groups describe comparable aggregated market data products by identifying their sources rather than specifying message formats or field-level content, as discussed below. By way of background, the Cboe One Feed is currently offered in two versions, Cboe One Summary and Cboe One Premium, each of which contains information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds and from the SIPs. The versions differ only in the quotation information each provides. Cboe One Summary provides the aggregate best bid and offer of all displayed orders, and Cboe One Premium provides aggregated two- sided quotations at multiple price levels, currently up to twelve per side per exchange. Execution information, administrative messages, and consolidated market information are the same in both versions. The current Cboe One Feed includes the following information from the Multicast Depth Feeds: individual last sale information for the Exchange and each of its affiliated exchanges, as well as Symbol Summary, Market Status, Retail Liquidity Identifier, Trading Status, and Trade Break messages. It also includes the following information from the SIPs: consolidated volume, the primary listing market's official opening and closing price, and the current day consolidated high and low price for all listed equity securities. The Cboe One Feed also disseminates the following information obtained from the Multicast Depth Feeds: the Cboe One Opening Price and Cboe One Closing Price. For BZX Listed securities, the Cboe One Opening Price is the BZX Official Opening Price as defined in Rule 11.23(a)(5), and the Cboe One Closing Price is the BZX Official Closing Price as defined in Rule 11.23(a)(3). For securities not listed on the Exchange, the Cboe One Opening Price is the first last sale eligible trade that occurs on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the Cboe One Closing Price is the final last sale eligible trade to occur on the Exchange or any of its affiliated exchanges prior to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Fees at Equity 7, To Establish an Optional Nasdaq PSX Monthly Subscription Fee Program
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Fees at Equity 7, To Establish an Optional Nasdaq PSX Monthly Subscription Fee Program

1. Purpose The purpose of the proposed rule change is to amend the Exchange's fee schedule at Equity 7, by establishing an optional Nasdaq PSX Monthly Subscription Fee Program. The rule text for the Program will be located in Section 3 of Equity 7. The Exchange is proposing to establish the Program as a completely voluntary and optional monthly alternative to its regular fee schedule, which charges firms separate fees for each product or service they consume, including per share executed fees for removing liquidity on the Exchange during the month. Although the existing fee schedule is competitive and works well for many firms, the Exchange observes that for some firms, the existing fee schedule fails to incentivize increased participation on the Exchange. To address this concern, and to make participation in the Exchange more predictable and ultimately more attractive, the Exchange proposes to offer its firms the option to pay a single subscription fee each month. Under the Program, a firm would be charged a flat fee of $650,000 a month. This fee will include an allocation of up to five order entry ports (i.e. OUCH, FIX, RASH) on Nasdaq PSX. It will also include liquidity-removing executions on Nasdaq PSX during the month--up to and including 0.125% of Consolidated Volume in the prior month (rounded up to the nearest whole share). Any liquidity- removing executions during the month on Nasdaq PSX that exceed 0.125% of Consolidated Volume in the prior month (rounded up to the nearest whole share) will be charged a fee of $0.0027 per share. Participation in the Program will not affect a firm's ability to earn rebates for providing liquidity on the Exchange. The Program would be entirely voluntary and optional. Any firm that does not sign up for the Program will be charged the default rates under Section 3 of Equity 7. To sign up for the Program, a firm must notify the Exchange before noon (Eastern Time) on the last trading day of the prior month. Likewise, a firm may withdraw from the Program by notifying the Exchange before noon (Eastern Time) on the last trading day of the prior month. A firm will remain enrolled in the Program unless it notifies the Exchange of its withdrawal from the same. The Exchange designed this fee to reflect the existing liquidity- removing execution and order entry protocol use of its firms, while also providing a cost-effective pathway for them to grow their participation on Nasdaq PSX. For firms whose current and expected activity aligns with this subscription fee model, the program could offer meaningful monthly savings compared with the existing regular fee schedule as their activity on Nasdaq PSX continues to grow. That said, each firm should evaluate for itself its expected needs and activities to determine whether the subscription fee or the regular fee schedule is appropriate. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange's proposed changes to its fee schedule are reasonable in several respects. As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for equity securities transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. The fact that this market is competitive has long been recognized by the courts. In NetCoalition v. Securities and Exchange Commission, the D.C. Circuit stated as follows: ``[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce .' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .'' The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system ``has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.'' Numerous indicia demonstrate the competitive nature of this market. For example, clear substitutes to the Exchange exist in the market for equity security transaction services. The Exchange is only one of several equity venues to which market participants may direct their order flow. Competing equity exchanges offer similar tiered pricing structures to that of the Exchange, including schedules of rebates and fees that apply based upon members achieving certain volume thresholds. Within this environment, market participants can freely and often do shift their order flow among the Exchange and competing venues in response to changes in their respective pricing schedules. As such, the proposal represents a reasonable attempt by the Exchange to increase its liquidity and market share relative to its competitors. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Increase the Exchange's Options Regulatory Fee (ORF)

1. Purpose At this time, PHLX proposes to increase the ORF rate from $0.0080 to $0.0090 per contract side, effective November 1, 2026. This rate change is influenced by a review of regulatory costs and realized options volumes at the Exchange. Additionally, the Exchange proposes a non-substantive change to Options 7, Section 6(D), to delete obsolete rule text that described a prior ORF collection methodology. PHLX assesses ORF for options transactions cleared by The Options Clearing Corporation (``OCC'') in the customer range, however ORF is assessed to each PHLX member organization for executions that occur on PHLX. Specifically, the ORF is collected by OCC on behalf of PHLX from member organizations and non-member organizations for all customer transactions executed on PHLX. ORF is assessed and collected on ultimately cleared customer contracts, taking into account adjustments for CMTA that were provided to PHLX the same day as the trade. Further, the Exchange bills ORF according to the clearing instructions provided on the execution. More specifically, PHLX assesses ORF based on the clearing instruction provided on the execution on trade date and does not take into consideration CMTA changes or transfers that occur at OCC. PHLX ensures that ORF Regulatory Revenue does not exceed a material portion of Options Regulatory Costs. More specifically, PHLX endeavors to ensure that ORF Regulatory Revenue generated from ORF does not exceed 82% of Options Regulatory Costs. The Exchange will notify member organizations via an Options Trader Alert of any change in the amount of the fee at least 30 calendar days prior to the effective date of the change. As is the case today, PHLX will monitor ORF Regulatory Revenue to ensure that it, in combination with other regulatory fees and fines, does not exceed Options Regulatory Costs. In determining whether an expense is considered an Options Regulatory Costs, the Exchange will continue to review all costs and make determinations whether there is a nexus between the expense and a regulatory function. The Exchange notes that fines collected by the Exchange in connection with a disciplinary matter will continue to offset Options Regulatory Costs. ORF Regulatory Revenue is designed to recover a material portion of the Options Regulatory Costs to the Exchange for the supervision and regulation of member organizations' transactions, including performing routine surveillances, investigations, examinations, financial monitoring, and policy, rulemaking, interpretive, and enforcement activities. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule General 8 Regarding Fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule General 8 Regarding Fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule General 8, Section 1(b) to provide that the installation fee and ongoing monthly fee for interfirm cabinet connectivity will apply separately to each of the two customers connected through an interfirm cabinet connectivity connection, as described below. Currently, the Exchange assesses the applicable installation fee and ongoing monthly fee only to the customer that submits the order. The other customer that accepts and participates in the connection is not separately assessed those fees. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new interfirm cabinet connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For interfirm cabinet connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change. Background The Exchange's data center campus consists of the original data center (``NY11''), an initial expansion area (``NY11-4''), and a second expansion area (``NY11-5'') (collectively, the ``Data Center'' or ``Data Center Campus''). Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is a fiber- based connectivity service that links cabinets used by two different colocation customers (``Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity'') throughout the Data Center Campus. The interfirm cabinet connection consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point: one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq-provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet. Before the Exchange implemented equalized connectivity throughout its Data Center, a customer would order Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity through the Nasdaq customer portal and identify the customer to which the ordering customer wanted to connect, with the ordering customer being solely responsible for both the installation and the ongoing monthly fiber connectivity fees. No separate installation or ongoing monthly fees were assessed, or are currently assessed, to the non-ordering customer for its side of the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity. With respect to provision and installation of the service, the fiber for the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity was provided and installed by a third-party provider or by the customer. The Exchange did not provide or install such fiber or manage such services. Equalization places greater emphasis on the way Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is supervised and managed, with Nasdaq taking a more central role in those functions. While customers still request the interfirm cabinet connection through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, the pre-existing fiber in the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity has been replaced with Exchange-provided, equalized fiber. Under this structure, the Exchange supervises and audits the interfirm cabinet connection on an ongoing basis. As discussed above, the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point: one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq- provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq- provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet. The Exchange provides and manages the cabling and standardized demarcation points and performs inventory management, implementation support, ongoing maintenance, monitoring, audit, and operational oversight for the connection. Both customers must act before the connection is implemented: one customer initiates the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity order through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, and the other customer accepts it. If the second customer does not accept the order, the connection is not implemented. Each participating customer consequently receives a distinct customer-side leg of a Nasdaq-provided, Nasdaq-managed, equalized connectivity path. Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is optional and is not required for a customer to obtain colocation services or to connect to the Exchange's trading systems. Proposal The Exchange proposes to retain the existing installation and ongoing monthly fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity and extend their application to the non-ordering, accepting customer side of the connection. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change. The Exchange anticipates implementing the proposed rule change during the first quarter of 2027 and will announce that implementation date through an Equity Trader Alert or other customer communication. The Exchange believes that assessing the existing fees separately to each customer appropriately reflects the Exchange's increased role in managing Data Center connectivity following Equalization. The Exchange now provides the fiber and manages, supervises, monitors, and audits the connection after installation. The proposal also aligns the allocation of fees with the structure of the service: two separately provided and managed customer-side legs join at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and each customer must authorize and receive the benefit of its own leg. The proposal therefore assesses each customer for the Nasdaq-provided and Nasdaq-managed connectivity furnished to that customer. 2. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend FINRA Rule 6121.02 Concerning the Resumption of Trading Following a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker Halt in Connection With the Industry's Expansion of Trading Hours to 23 Hours Per Day, 5 Days Per Week

1. Purpose FINRA proposes to amend FINRA Rule 6121.02 concerning the resumption of trading following a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker (``MWCB'') halt (``Level 3 Market Decline'') in connection with the industry's expansion of trading hours to 23 hours per day, 5 days per week (``23/5 Trading''). As discussed herein, the proposed rule change would retain the current 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time (``E.T.'') resumption time following a Level 3 Market Decline. Background The MWCB mechanism under FINRA Rule 6121.02 provides an important, automatic mechanism that is invoked to promote stability and investor confidence during a period of significant stress when U.S. securities markets experience extreme broad-based declines. FINRA and all U.S. equity exchanges (collectively, the self-regulatory organizations or ``SROs'') adopted uniform rules relating to market-wide circuit breakers in 2012, which are designed to slow the effects of extreme price movement through coordinated trading halts across U.S. securities markets when severe price declines reach levels that may exhaust market liquidity. Such market-wide circuit breakers provide for trading halts in all U.S. equities and options markets during a severe market decline as measured by a single-day decline in the S&P 500 Index during regular trading hours. Pursuant to Rule 6121.02, a market-wide trading halt will be triggered if the S&P 500 Index declines in price by specified percentages from the prior day's closing price of that index. Currently, the triggers are set at three circuit breaker thresholds: 7% (Level 1), 13% (Level 2), and 20% (Level 3). A market decline that triggers a Level 1 or Level 2 halt after 9:30 a.m. E.T. and before 3:25 p.m. E.T. would halt market-wide trading for 15 minutes, while a similar market decline at or after 3:25 p.m. E.T. would not halt market-wide trading. If a Level 3 Market Decline occurs at any time during the trading day, trading otherwise than on an exchange in all NMS stocks will halt for the remainder of the trading day. Proposal FINRA now proposes to amend Rule 6121.02 to reflect extended trading hours under 23/5 Trading. On December 6, 2026, several exchanges intend to offer new overnight trading sessions that would be available from 9:00 p.m. E.T. to 4:00 a.m. E.T. As discussed, consistent with the uniform rules in place across all SROs, current Rule 6121.02(c)(2) provides that, if a Level 3 Market Decline occurs at any time during the trading day, trading otherwise than on an exchange in all NMS stocks will halt for the remainder of the trading day. Currently, that means that the earliest that any SRO would permit trading to resume after a Level 3 Market Decline is 4:00 a.m. E.T. the following day, since no SROs are open for trading before 4:00 a.m. E.T. Unless amended, when 23/5 Trading is launched, the current rule's reference to halting ``for the remainder of the trading day'' would permit trading to resume at an earlier time, i.e., 9:00 p.m. E.T. on the same calendar day, when some SROs' systems would generally become available for overnight trading. FINRA does not believe that this is an expected or desired result and is therefore amending this rule in coordination with the other SROs such that trading will not resume until 4:00 a.m. E.T. or later on the following trading day, consistent with current market practice. This proposed rule change is not intended to make any substantive changes to the MWCB mechanism. Rather, the proposed rule change would preserve the current resumption time following a Level 3 Market Decline. To effect this change, FINRA proposes to delete the language in Rule 6121.02(c)(2) that provides that FINRA shall halt trading otherwise than on an exchange in all NMS stocks ``for the remainder of the trading day'' if a Level 3 Market Decline occurs at any time during the trading day, and replace it with new language that explicitly provides that FINRA shall halt trading otherwise than on an exchange in all NMS stocks until 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time or later on the following trading day. FINRA has filed the proposed rule change for immediate effectiveness. The implementation date of the proposed rule change will be December 6, 2026. 2. Statutory Basis FINRA believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 15A(b)(6) of the Act, which requires, among other things, that FINRA rules be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The MWCB mechanism described in Rule 6121.02 is an important, automatic mechanism that is invoked to promote stability and investor confidence during a period of significant stress when securities markets experience extreme broad-based declines. The proposed rule change, when applied uniformly by all SROs, would ensure that the current 4:00 a.m. E.T. resumption time following a Level 3 halt continues to apply under 23/5 Trading, notwithstanding current rule text implying that the resumption time would coincide with the start of overnight trading on SROs operating an overnight session. Rather than leave the rule in place as is, which would result in an earlier resumption time than originally contemplated when the rule was adopted, FINRA and the U.S. equity exchanges met alongside industry representatives to determine the appropriate resumption time. Following those discussions, the collective decision was made to retain the 4:00 a.m. E.T. resumption time, notwithstanding the fact that an earlier resumption time would be possible with the introduction of 23/5 Trading. The proposed rule change codifies this decision into FINRA's rules. FINRA understands that the other SROs have filed or will also be filing similar proposed rule changes. 1. Purpose Background The Exchange adopted a warrant performance incentive program (``Program'') to allow Members of the Exchange who participate in the Program (``Participants'') to earn the right to purchase Non-Voting Common Units of 24X US Holdings LLC (``24X US Holdco''), the Exchange's parent company. As described in the Warrant Program Releases, each Member of the Exchange may become a Participant in the Program by prepaying $250,000 or $500,000 in Exchange fees (``Prepayment Fee'') and satisfying the Program eligibility requirements. Upon joining the Program, each Participant will receive a warrant that vests based on the Participant's achievement of certain minimum trading volumes (``Target Volume'') on the Exchange during each designated pre-determined period in which the Program is in effect (``Measurement Period''). When the warrants vest, Participants will have the right to exercise the warrants to purchase a certain number of 24X US Holdco Non-Voting Common Units. 24X Overnight Trading The Target Volume may be met by trading activity in any security traded on 24X. Participants that trade securities on 24X during 24X Overnight Trading--defined in the Warrant Program Release as a trading session in which trading is permitted during the period from 8 p.m. ET to 9:30 a.m. ET for each overnight period except for Friday to Saturday and Saturday to Sunday --will receive quintuple credit (i.e., multiplied by five) (``5X Overnight Multiplier'') for such trading for purposes of calculating the Participant's performance during the Measurement Period. A cap of 50% of the Target Volume (post the 5X Overnight Multiplier) will be placed on trading contributions during 24X Overnight Trading, such that any overnight trades executed beyond the cap will not be counted toward a Participant's Target Volume. The Exchange has determined to revise the Program to clarify that 24X Overnight Trading will begin at 9:00 p.m. ET instead of 8:00 p.m. ET. At the time of the Warrant Program Release, the Exchange's rules provided that the 24X Market Session (the Exchange's overnight trading session) would begin at 8:00 p.m. ET. Since then, the Exchange has revised its rules to reflect that the Post-Market Session will end at 8:00 p.m. ET and the 24X Market Session will begin at 9:00 p.m. ET. Therefore, the Exchange is making this change to align the terms of the Program with the revised schedule of the Exchange's trading sessions. The Exchange has further determined to revise the Program to allow any trading that occurs during 24X Overnight Trading beyond the 50% Target Volume cap to still count toward a Participant's Target Volume on a one-to-one basis. Currently, the Program contemplates that trades executed overnight will be eligible for the 5X Overnight Multiplier until the 50% Target Volume cap is reached, and then no additional overnight trades will be counted toward a Participant's Target Volume. In order to encourage liquidity provision during 24X Overnight Trading, the Exchange is revising the Program so that additional overnight trades beyond the 50% Target Volume cap will be counted toward a Participant's Target Volume, but will not be eligible for the 5X Overnight Multiplier. Maintaining the 50% Target Volume cap on the number of overnight trades that are eligible for the 5X Overnight Multiplier will ensure that daytime liquidity still remains strong. Sponsored Participant Prepayment Fee A recent amendment to the Program also allows a Sponsored Participant, as defined in Exchange Rules 1.5(ee) and 11.3(b), to be a joint Participant in the Program together with a Sponsoring Member of the Exchange, so long as the Sponsored Participant: (i) fulfills the provisions of Exchange Rule 11.3(b); (ii) qualifies as an ``accredited investor'' as such term is defined in Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933; (iii) has executed the required documentation for participation in the Program (the subscription agreement, warrant agreement, and confidentiality agreement, each between the Sponsored Participant and the Exchange); (iv) has caused to be tendered (by the Sponsoring Member) the Prepayment Fee no later than the first day of each calendar quarter of the Program Period to participate in the Program as of such quarter; and (v) has identifiable trading volume on the Exchange that is directly attributable to the Sponsored Participant. In order to reduce the barrier to entry for prospective Sponsored Participants that desire to participate in the Program, the Exchange has also determined to revise the Program to allow Sponsored Participants that jointly participate in the Program together with a Sponsoring Member to tender the Prepayment Fee directly to the Exchange on their own behalf, rather than causing the Prepayment Fee to be tendered by the Sponsoring Member. All other terms regarding the Prepayment Fee would remain unchanged as described in the Warrant Program Releases. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Depository Trust Company; Notice of Filing of Partial Amendment No. 1 and Notice of Designation of Longer Period for Commission Action on Proposed Rule Change To Establish and Implement AnnounceDirect for the Submission of Corporate Action Announcements

Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Depository Trust Company; Notice of Filing of Partial Amendment No. 1 and Notice of Designation of Longer Period for Commission Action on Proposed Rule Change To Establish and Implement AnnounceDirect for the Submission of Corporate Action Announcements

I. Introduction On September 15, 2026, the Depository Trust Company (``DTC'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'') proposed rule change DTC-2026-010, pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder. The proposed rule change was published for public comment in the Federal Register on September 29, 2026. The Commission has received comments regarding the substance of the changes proposed. On November 6, 2026, DTC filed Partial Amendment No. 1 to modify the proposed rule change (the proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, is hereinafter referred to as the ``proposed rule change''). The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on Partial Amendment No. 1 from interested persons and to designate a longer time period for Commission action on the proposed rule change. II. Description of Partial Amendment No. 1 In Partial Amendment No. 1, DTC revises the implementation timeframe for the first phase of AnnounceDirect from November 2026 to no later than March 31, 2027 and states that DTC would announce the specific implementation date by Important Notice at least 14 days in advance. III. Solicitation of Comments Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Exchange Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods: Electronic Comments Use the Commission's internet comment form (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml); or Send an email to [email protected]. Please include file number SR-DTC-2026-010 on the subject line. Paper Comments Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549. All submissions should refer to file number SR-DTC-2026-010. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of DTC and on DTCC's website (https://dtcc.com/legal/sec-rule-filings.aspx). Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-DTC-2026-010 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026. IV. Designation of Longer Period for Commission Action Section 19(b)(2)(i) of the Exchange Act provides that, within 45 days of the publication of notice of the filing of a proposed rule change, the Commission shall either approve the proposed rule change, disapprove the proposed rule change, or institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be disapproved unless the Commission extends the period within which it must act as provided in Section 19(b)(2)(ii) of the Exchange Act. Section 19(b)(2)(ii) of the Exchange Act allows the Commission to designate a longer period for review (up to 90 days from the publication of notice of the filing of a proposed rule change) if the Commission finds such longer period to be appropriate and publishes its reasons for so finding, or as to which the self-regulatory organization consents. The 45th day after publication of the Notice of Filing is November 13, 2026. In order to provide the Commission with sufficient time to consider the proposed rule change, the Commission finds that it is appropriate to designate a longer period within which to take action on the proposed rule change and therefore is extending this 45-day time period. Accordingly, the Commission, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Exchange Act, designates December 28, 2026, as the date by which the Commission shall either approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings to determine whether to disapprove proposed rule change SR-DTC-2026- 010. 17 CFR 200.30-3(a)(12). --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Sherry R. Haywood, Assistant Secretary. [FR Doc. 2026-23337 Filed 11-16-26; 8:45 am] BILLING CODE 8011-01-P

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend its Price List

Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend its Price List

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Price List to modify the share threshold requirement for free late D Orders at the close. The Exchange proposes to implement the fee changes effective November 2, 2026. Background and Proposed Rule Change Currently, in the section of the Price List headed ``Executions at the Close,'' the Exchange offers fees differentiated by time of entry (or last modification) for D Orders at the close by a member organization. Specifically, for member organizations with an ADV of at least 10,000 shares entered and executed by an affiliated Floor broker, D Orders are free up to specific monthly levels, which for Late D Orders is currently the first 10,000,000 shares. Above that threshold, member organizations with Adding ADV of at least 0.50% of Tape A CADV and total close activity of at least 1.75% of Tape A CADV are charged $0.0011 per share; all other member organizations are charged $0.0012 per share. The Exchange proposes to increase the volume threshold applicable to Late D Orders. As proposed, qualifying member organizations would not be charged for the first 15,000,000 shares of Late D Orders. The existing rate for Late D Orders applicable to volume above that threshold would remain unchanged. The Exchange believes that the proposed change would further encourage additional liquidity on the Exchange, particularly in the Closing Auction. The Exchange notes that several member organizations could benefit from the proposed higher threshold given their current D Order volumes. By increasing the amount of Late D Order volume that may be executed without charge, the Exchange believes that these member organizations would have an additional incentive to submit additional D Orders to the Closing Auction in order to take advantage of the enhanced pricing opportunity. As a result, the Exchange expects the proposal to attract additional liquidity and order flow to the Closing Auction, improving execution opportunities for all market participants. The Exchange further believes that member organizations derive significant value from participating in the Exchange's Closing Auction, a recognized industry benchmark for the pricing and valuation of numerous indices, funds, and derivative products. Increased participation in the Closing Auction contributes to the quality of the auction process by enhancing liquidity, promoting price discovery, and increasing the opportunity for orders to receive executions at the Exchange's closing price. Moreover, because member organizations closely track the adding volumes they submit to the Exchange, the Exchange believes that they can readily determine at the time of execution whether their Late D Orders will execute free of charge or be subject to the current fee set forth in the Price List. Accordingly, the proposal would provide certainty regarding the applicable fees at the time of execution and promote the efficient use of Exchange systems. The proposed changes are not otherwise intended to address other issues, and the Exchange is not aware of any significant problems that market participants would have in complying with the proposed changes. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and (5) of the Act, in particular, because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members, issuers and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers. The Proposed Change Is Reasonable The Exchange believes that the proposal to increase the volume threshold for Late D Orders so that qualifying member organizations would not be charged for the first 15,000,000 shares of Late D Orders is reasonable. The Exchange believes that the proposal would encourage additional liquidity on the Exchange, especially during the Closing Auction, thereby contributing to robust levels of liquidity on the Floor and at the close, to the benefit of all market participants. The Exchange further believes that increased trading volumes contribute to the quality of the Closing Auction by improving execution opportunities for participants seeking to transact at the close, which benefits all market participants. In addition, the proposal is designed to attract higher volumes of orders from member organizations, which would promote greater price discovery and increased trading opportunities on the Exchange, both intraday and during the Closing Auction. The Exchange also believes that encouraging additional liquidity and order flow for execution on the trading Floor in the Closing Auction would strengthen the Exchange's competitive position and market share relative to its competitors. As noted, there are several member organizations that could benefit from the proposed higher threshold given their current D Order volumes, and the Exchange believes that increasing the amount of D Orders that are not charged a fee would incentivize those member organizations to enter additional D Orders in the Closing Auction in order to take advantage of the higher threshold. The Exchange's closing auction is a recognized industry benchmark, and member organizations receive a substantial benefit from the Exchange in obtaining high levels of executions at the Exchange's closing price on a daily basis. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Adopt a Broker-Dealer Clearing Member Incentive Program and Reduce the Clearing Fee for Securities Contracts

Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Adopt a Broker-Dealer Clearing Member Incentive Program and Reduce the Clearing Fee for Securities Contracts

1. Purpose CCUS proposes to amend its Fee Schedule to adopt the BD Program in connection with its issuance and clearance of Securities Contracts, and to reduce the clearing fee for Securities Contracts. Market Makers and other broker-dealers trading for their own proprietary accounts are critical for options to have liquid and active markets. These market participants generally clear securities options transactions through separate clearing firms, including, in the case of broker-dealers, transactions for proprietary accounts of broker-dealers (``PAB'' transactions). Therefore, for Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts issued by CCUS to be cleared, CCUS Clearing Members must be able and eligible to clear Securities Contracts. Before a clearing firm can clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts at CCUS, CCUS understands a clearing firm must complete significant back-office development work, including system development, connectivity to CCUS, risk and margin integration, testing and certification, and operational readiness. Clearing firms have many competing items in their development queues. To incentivize clearing firms to prioritize in the near term the work needed to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts at CCUS, CCUS proposes to adopt the BD Program. Eligibility and Selection CCUS may select BD Clearing Members (or prospective BD Clearing Members) to participate in the BD Program. To be eligible, a firm must: (1) notify CCUS of its intent to participate in the BD Program no later than November 11, 2026, in a form and manner prescribed by CCUS; and (2) be a BD Clearing Member or a prospective BD Clearing Member at the time it provides such notice. CCUS will select BD Program participants from among eligible firms by considering the following factors: (1) adequacy of capital, (2) operational capacity, (3) clearing experience, (4) regulatory history, and (5) other relevant factors CCUS believes demonstrate the firm's capacity to engage in the clearing of Securities Contracts. CCUS believes it is reasonable to limit participation in the BD Program to clearing firms that can demonstrate they possess the resources to be operationally ready to clear Securities Contracts at CCUS in a compressed time period (as early as the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, as discussed below). Regardless of participation in the BD Program, any BD Clearing Member (or prospective BD Clearing Member, once approved) may clear Securities Contracts through CCUS at any time those contracts are trading on a national securities exchange. Standards and Payments If, by the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, a BD Program participant (1) is a BD Clearing Member in good standing with CCUS that has satisfied applicable documentation and operational requirements prescribed by CCUS and completed connectivity and certification testing for clearing Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts cleared by CCUS, and (2) submits written documentation evidencing readiness to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts cleared by CCUS, each in a manner prescribed by CCUS, the BD Program participant will receive a one-time payment of $1,250,000. If a BD Program participant does not satisfy the above criteria by the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, but does so by November 25, 2026, the BD Program participant will instead receive a one-time payment of $750,000. If a BD Program participant does not satisfy the above criteria by November 25, 2026, but does so by November 30, 2026, the BD Program participant will instead receive a one-time payment of $500,000. Clearing Fee Reduction CCUS also proposes to reduce the clearing fee for Securities Contracts set forth in the clearing fees table on the Fee Schedule from $0.002 per cleared contract to $0.001 per cleared contract. The reduced fee will apply equally to all transactions. CCUS proposes the reduction to lower the cost of clearing transactions at CCUS. 2. Statutory Basis CCUS believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a registered clearing agency and, in particular, Section 17A(b)(3) of the Act. Specifically, CCUS believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(D) of the Act, which requires that the rules of a clearing agency provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its participants. CCUS also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act, which requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a national system for the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and that they not be designed to permit unfair discrimination in the admission of participants or among participants in the use of the clearing agency. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing of Proposed Change Amending Section 341 of the NYSE American Company Guide To Address Multi-Step Transactions

Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing of Proposed Change Amending Section 341 of the NYSE American Company Guide To Address Multi-Step Transactions

1. Purpose Section 341 (``Acquisition of a Listed Issuer by an Unlisted Entity'') of the Company Guide provides that, if a listed issuer engages in a Reverse Merger, it will be eligible for continued listing on the Exchange only if the post-transaction entity meets the standards for initial listing. Section 341 provides that the Exchange will refuse to list additional securities of a listed issuer in connection with a Reverse Merger unless the post-transaction entity meets the standards for initial listing and the listed issuer obtains shareholder approval of the issuance of such securities as required by Section 713(b) of the Company Guide. In recent times, a small number of companies listed on the Exchange have structured a Reverse Merger as a multi-step transaction. In a multi-step reverse merger, in connection with the consummation of a merger with the unlisted entity, the listed company issues to the owner of the unlisted entity (i) a number of shares of the listed company's common stock that would not require shareholder approval under Section 713(b) or give rise to a change of control and (ii) additional consideration in the form of contingently convertible securities that will become convertible into common stock upon subsequent receipt of approval of the listed company's shareholders. The owners of the unlisted entity obtain control of the post-merger entity only upon the later conversion of the contingently convertible securities into common stock. The Exchange notes that the definition of ``Reverse Merger'' for purposes of Section 341 and the requirements of the rule only apply when the change of control occurs. As such, under Section 341 as currently drafted, a listed issuer may consummate the merger in a multi-step reverse merger transaction even if the combined entity would not meet the Exchange's initial listing standards. In such a case, the Exchange would have no choice but to permit the consummation of the merger and then delist the company in the event that the shareholders approve the conversion of the contingently convertible securities and the combined entity proceeds with conversion and does not meet the initial listing standards at the time of that conversion. In some cases, a company may refrain from converting the contingently convertible securities in order to avoid delisting, leaving the company in the unusual position of having completed a merger without effectuating the change of control that was anticipated when the merger agreement was reached. The Exchange wishes to address the effect under Section 341 of structuring a Reverse Merger using the multi-step reverse merger structure. The Exchange proposes to amend Section 341 to define a Multi-Step Reverse Merger for purposes of that rule as a transaction in which a listed issuer engages in a Reverse Merger through a series of transactions, where the listed issuer enters into an agreement with an unlisted entity that provides for an initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer, along with the anticipated future issuance of additional shares of the listed issuer upon conversion, exchange or exercise of securities of another type of the listed issuer when the future issuance of the shares would result in a change of control of the listed issuer. The Exchange proposes to amend Section 341 to provide that in a Multi-Step Reverse Merger, the listed issuer will be eligible for continued listing on the Exchange only if, at the time of the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer, the contemplated post- transaction entity meets initial listing standards. The revised rule will specify that, in determining the post-transaction entity's compliance with initial listing standards in a Multi-Step Reverse Merger, the Exchange will assume the issuance of all shares anticipated to be issued upon conversion, exchange or exercise of securities as part of the Multi-Step Reverse Merger. Section 341 provides that the Exchange should be consulted whenever a listed issuer is contemplating a transaction or series of transactions that could constitute a Reverse Merger. If the Exchange determines that a transaction or series of transactions constitute a Reverse Merger, the listed issuer must submit an initial listing application for the post-transaction entity with sufficient time to allow the Exchange to complete its review before the effective date of the Reverse Merger. The proposed amended form of Section 341 will provide that the listed issuer must submit the required initial listing application prior to the Reverse Merger or the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer in the Multi-Step Reverse Merger, as the case may be. In its current form, Section 341 states that ``in determining whether a change of control constitutes a Reverse Merger, the Exchange will consider all relevant factors, including, but not limited to, changes in the management, board of directors, voting power, ownership, and financial structure of the listed issuer.'' The Exchange proposes to clarify this statement by modifying it to state that the Exchange will undertake this analysis of all relevant factors ``in considering whether a change of control has occurred in the context of a Reverse Merger.'' Section 341 contains a sentence providing that if the initial listing application has not been approved prior to the effective date of the Reverse Merger, the Exchange will issue a Staff Determination Letter as set forth in Section 1202 and begin delisting proceedings pursuant to Part 12. The Exchange proposes to amend this sentence to state that if the initial listing application has not been approved prior to the effective date of the Reverse Merger or the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer in the Multi-Step Reverse Merger, as the case may be, the Exchange will issue a Staff Determination Letter and begin delisting proceedings. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; MIAX Sapphire, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange Fee Schedule To Exclude Options Volume Executed During Extended Trading Hours From Calculations Applicable for Certain Fees, Rebates, and Discounts

Self-Regulatory Organizations; MIAX Sapphire, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange Fee Schedule To Exclude Options Volume Executed During Extended Trading Hours From Calculations Applicable for Certain Fees, Rebates, and Discounts

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non- transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. Exchange Rule 501 describes the Exchange's hours of operation. In particular, the hours during which option transactions may be made on the Exchange shall be from 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time except for option contracts on Exchange Traded Fund Shares, as defined in Rule 402(i), and Index-Linked Securities, as defined in Rule 402(k)(1), which may remain open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time, as designated by the Exchange. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq ISE, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Rules at Options 7, Section 6 (Other Options Fees and Rebates)

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Pricing Schedule at Options 7, Section 6 (Other Options Fees and Rebates). Currently, the Exchange offers a PIM rebate of $0.105 per contract to Electronic Access Members that utilize PIM to execute more than 0.75% of Priority Customer volume in Regular Orders, calculated as a percentage of Customer Total Consolidated Volume per day in a given month. As used in the Pricing Schedule, ``Priority Customer'' includes ``Retail,'' as defined in Options 7, Section 1(c), and Customer Total Consolidated Volume means the total national volume cleared at The Options Clearing Corporation in the Customer range in equity and ETF options in that month. The rebate is paid for Priority Customer Regular Orders under 250 contracts that are submitted to PIM. The Exchange proposes to modify the amount of this rebate, from $0.105 per contract, to $0.10 per contract. The Exchange is not otherwise modifying the eligibility, calculation, payment, aggregation, or exclusion provisions applicable to this rebate. The Exchange believes the revised rebate will continue to encourage qualifying Electronic Access Members to submit smaller-sized Priority Customer Regular Orders to PIM for price improvement while allowing the Exchange to periodically adjust its incentive programs. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system ``has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.'' Likewise, in NetCoalition v. Securities and Exchange Commission (``NetCoalition'') the D.C. Circuit upheld the Commission's use of a market-based approach in evaluating the fairness of market data fees against a challenge claiming that Congress mandated a cost-based approach. As the court emphasized, the Commission ``intended in Regulation NMS that `market forces, rather than regulatory requirements' play a role in determining the market data . . . to be made available to investors and at what cost.'' Further, ``[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .'' Although the court and the SEC were discussing the cash equities markets, the Exchange believes that these views apply with equal force to the options markets. The Exchange believes that its proposal to reduce the PIM rebate in Options 7, Section 6.C from $0.105 per contract to $0.10 per contract is reasonable. The Exchange has limited resources to allocate to its incentive programs and periodically assesses its fee structure to ensure that its rebates continue to attract order flow while remaining sustainable. The proposed rebate of $0.10 per contract represents only a modest reduction from the current $0.105 per contract level, and the Exchange believes that this rebate remains attractive and will continue to incentivize qualifying Electronic Access Members to submit smaller- sized Priority Customer Regular Orders to PIM for price improvement, which benefits all market participants. The Exchange believes that its proposal to reduce the PIM rebate is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the modified rebate will apply uniformly to all Electronic Access Members that satisfy the objective volume qualification (utilizing PIM to execute more than 0.75% of Priority Customer volume in Regular Orders, calculated as a percentage of Customer Total Consolidated Volume per day in a given month) with respect to all Priority Customer Regular Orders under 250 contracts submitted to PIM. Any Electronic Access Member is able to qualify for the rebate by meeting the applicable volume threshold, and all qualifying Members will receive the same $0.10 per contract rebate on such orders. Any Electronic Access Member may participate in PIM, and Market Makers may respond to a PIM. While the rebate is targeted at Priority Customer Regular Orders, this does not render the proposal unfairly discriminatory because Priority Customers pay no Fees for PIM Orders and Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers, and increased Market Maker activity facilitates tighter spreads that may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fees Schedule To Clarify That Fee Codes BC, BM, BN and BO Apply to the Russell 2000 Index (“RUT”)
