Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fees Schedule To Clarify That Fee Codes BC, BM, BN and BO Apply to the Russell 2000 Index (“RUT”)

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule, effective November 2, 2026, to clarify that fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO apply to options on the Russell 2000 Index (``RUT''). Currently, fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the ``Fee Codes and Associated Fees'' table do not expressly reference RUT. The Exchange proposes to amend the Fees Schedule to add RUT to fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the ``Fee Codes and Associated Fees'' table to clarify that these are the fees specifically charged for RUT. The Exchange notes that these fee codes (BC, BM, BN and BO) are already used in a prior table that expressly calls out the applicable fees for executions in RUT. This proposed change is only intended to provide clarity in the second instance where these fee codes are used within the Fee Schedule. The proposed change does not make any substantive changes to the amount of any fee or rebate set forth in the Fees Schedule, nor does it change how any fee or rebate is assessed. Rather, the proposed change is non- substantive and clarifying in nature and is intended to make the Fees Schedule more accurate and transparent. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the ``Act'') and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act, which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Trading Permit Holders and other persons using its facilities. The Exchange believes the proposed amendment to add RUT to fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the ``Fee Codes and Associated Fees'' table of the Fees Schedule is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory, and promotes just and equitable principles of trade, because it is a clarifying change that makes no substantive change to any fee amount. The proposed change will provide greater clarity and transparency in the Fees Schedule regarding the fee codes applicable to RUT transactions, thereby reducing potential confusion among market participants, which removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protects investors and the public interest. The proposed change applies equally to all Trading Permit Holders. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe the proposed change will impose any burden on intramarket competition. The proposed change is a clarifying, non-substantive change that adds ``RUT'' to the description for fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the Fees Schedule, does not change any fee amount, and applies equally to all Trading Permit Holders. The Exchange does not believe the proposed change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed change is not intended to address competitive issues, but rather is a clarifying change designed to improve the clarity and transparency of the Exchange's Fees Schedule C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change. III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved. IV. Solicitation of Comments Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change by The Options Clearing Corporation Concerning Providing the Ability To Satisfy Daily Margin Deficit Amounts With Non-Cash Collateral Prior To Settlement Time
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change by The Options Clearing Corporation Concerning Providing the Ability To Satisfy Daily Margin Deficit Amounts With Non-Cash Collateral Prior To Settlement Time

1. Purpose OCC proposes to change its Rules to provide Clearing Members with an opportunity to reduce or eliminate any margin deficit identified in the Daily Account Summary to avoid OCC's cash draw prior to Settlement Time. This change is expected to have positive effects on both OCC and Clearing Members. The current start-of-day margin cash settlement process often requires multiple inefficient transfers of collateral and cash during the trading day, resulting in temporary double- collateralization for Clearing Members. Presently, after OCC drafts cash from a Clearing Member's bank account prior to Settlement Time to satisfy a start-of-day-margin deficit, the Clearing Member often deposits non-cash collateral with OCC and requests that OCC return some or all of the cash back to the Clearing Member's bank account. OCC allows this intraday deposit of margin and returns the cash, but the process is inefficient for all parties. Under the current process, OCC must often make multiple cash transactions, drafting cash from Clearing Member accounts and then returning the cash to the Clearing Member on the same day. And because the cash transfer is not instantaneous, this series of events leaves Clearing Members double-collateralized for a period. Clearing Members may not receive their returned cash until hours after they deposited additional collateral, meaning that they are double-collateralized (through the newly deposited collateral and the cash that has not yet been returned) from the time when they deposit additional collateral until the previously drafted cash is returned to their bank accounts. This process increases cash liquidity demands on Clearing Members, causes Clearing Members to hold excess collateral to attempt to avoid daily deficit cash drafts, and increases instances of same-day double- collateralization. For OCC, this process increases transactional cash flows, causing unnecessary inefficiency and increased operational risk. These issues could be alleviated or eliminated if Clearing Members had the opportunity to deposit collateral to satisfy any identified margin deficit before OCC withdraws cash to satisfy the deficit. And regardless of whether a Clearing Member chooses to deposit additional margin, the ultimate Start-of-Day Margin Deficit and the corresponding deficit cash draft would be no greater than the deficit originally identified in the Daily Account Summary. A hypothetical example may demonstrate how the updated daily settlement process would work in practice. If OCC were to report on a Clearing Member's Daily Account Summary that the Clearing Member faced a margin deficit, the Clearing Member would be afforded the choice whether to offset that deficit, in whole or in part, by depositing collateral prior to OCC issuing cash settlement instructions to the Clearing Member's bank. If the Clearing Member were to choose not to deposit additional collateral, OCC would issue cash settlement instructions to the Clearing Member's bank to satisfy the deficit with cash from the Clearing Member's account. But if the Clearing Member were to deposit additional collateral before OCC issued cash settlement instructions to the bank, the newly deposited collateral would reduce or eliminate the amount that OCC would withdraw from the Clearing Member's bank account. If the proposed change is adopted, OCC will no longer immediately draft the full margin deficit from the Clearing Member's account in cash, but instead will give the Clearing Member the opportunity to satisfy or reduce the deficit with non-cash collateral before OCC conducts any cash draw from Clearing Member bank accounts. This reduces Clearing Members' need for cash liquidity, double-collateralization, and OCC's transactional cash flows and any attendant operational risk. OCC does not anticipate that this proposed change would negatively affect its liquidity. Start of day liquidity is unaffected because OCC will continue to withdraw cash from Clearing Member bank accounts by Settlement Time each day to satisfy any remaining margin deficits, just as it does in the current model. And intraday liquidity will be only minimally affected. In the current model when OCC withdraws cash to satisfy a margin deficit, most of the cash is returned to Clearing Members that same day after the Clearing Members deposit additional non-cash collateral. Finally, the proposed change affects only margin deficits; it will not affect how OCC handles money that flows daily through it from one party to another or how OCC collects mandatory margin cash requirements from time to time. For example, the settlement system by which OCC collects cash from one Clearing Member and passes it along to another Clearing Member would remain unchanged, as would the process for when a Clearing Member defaults. OCC will have qualified liquidity resources supported by all eligible forms of collateral both at the start of the day and intraday under the proposed change. Description of Change In order to provide Clearing Members with the opportunity to satisfy daily margin deficits with collateral prior to OCC initiating a cash draw from their bank accounts, OCC proposes to amend its Rules. In particular OCC proposes amendments to Rule 605 and the creation of a new Rule 605A to implement this change. OCC proposes to amend Rule 605 to change the name of the report Clearing Members receive identifying their margin deficit from ``Daily Margin Report'' to ``Daily Account Summary.'' This change is proposed to more accurately reflect the document that Clearing Members receive on a daily basis that identifies their margin deficit. OCC also proposes shortening and simplifying the rule by simply stating that the Daily Account Summary will show the margin required by the Clearing Member's ``margined positions,'' rather than listing each type of position that could require margin; however, the types of positions covered in the report will not change. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule General 8 Regarding Fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule General 8, Section 1(b) to provide that the installation fee and ongoing monthly fee for interfirm cabinet connectivity will apply separately to each of the two customers connected through an interfirm cabinet connectivity connection, as described below. Currently, the Exchange assesses the applicable installation fee and ongoing monthly fee only to the customer that submits the order. The other customer that accepts and participates in the connection is not separately assessed those fees. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new interfirm cabinet connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For interfirm cabinet connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change. Background The Exchange's data center campus consists of the original data center (``NY11''), an initial expansion area (``NY11-4''), and a second expansion area (``NY11-5'') (collectively, the ``Data Center'' or ``Data Center Campus''). Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is a fiber- based connectivity service that links cabinets used by two different colocation customers (``Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity'') throughout the Data Center Campus. The interfirm cabinet connection consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point: one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq-provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet. Before the Exchange implemented equalized connectivity throughout its Data Center, a customer would order Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity through the Nasdaq customer portal and identify the customer to which the ordering customer wanted to connect, with the ordering customer being solely responsible for both the installation and the ongoing monthly fiber connectivity fees. No separate installation or ongoing monthly fees were assessed, or are currently assessed, to the non-ordering customer for its side of the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity. With respect to provision and installation of the service, the fiber for the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity was provided and installed by a third-party provider or by the customer. The Exchange did not provide or install such fiber or manage such services. Equalization places greater emphasis on the way Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is supervised and managed, with Nasdaq taking a more central role in those functions. While customers still request the interfirm cabinet connection through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, the pre-existing fiber in the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity has been replaced with Exchange-provided, equalized fiber. Under this structure, the Exchange supervises and audits the interfirm cabinet connection on an ongoing basis. As discussed above, the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point: one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq- provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq- provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet. The Exchange provides and manages the cabling and standardized demarcation points and performs inventory management, implementation support, ongoing maintenance, monitoring, audit, and operational oversight for the connection. Both customers must act before the connection is implemented: one customer initiates the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity order through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, and the other customer accepts it. If the second customer does not accept the order, the connection is not implemented. Each participating customer consequently receives a distinct customer-side leg of a Nasdaq-provided, Nasdaq-managed, equalized connectivity path. Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is optional and is not required for a customer to obtain colocation services or to connect to the Exchange's trading systems. Proposal The Exchange proposes to retain the existing installation and ongoing monthly fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity and extend their application to the non-ordering, accepting customer side of the connection. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change. The Exchange anticipates implementing the proposed rule change during the first quarter of 2027 and will announce that implementation date through an Equity Trader Alert or other customer communication. The Exchange believes that assessing the existing fees separately to each customer appropriately reflects the Exchange's increased role in managing Data Center connectivity following Equalization. The Exchange now provides the fiber and manages, supervises, monitors, and audits the connection after installation. The proposal also aligns the allocation of fees with the structure of the service: two separately provided and managed customer-side legs join at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and each customer must authorize and receive the benefit of its own leg. The proposal therefore assesses each customer for the Nasdaq-provided and Nasdaq-managed connectivity furnished to that customer. 2. title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Revision: Ombudsman Matter Management System (OMMS) Form

Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Revision: Ombudsman Matter Management System (OMMS) Form

[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 220 (Tuesday, November 17, 2026)] [Notices] [Pages 73837-73838] From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov] [FR Doc No: 2026-23325] ----------------------------------------------------------------------- SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION [OMB Control No. 3235-0748] Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Revision: Ombudsman Matter Management System (OMMS) Form Upon Written Request, Copies Available From: Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of FOIA Services, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-2736 Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC or ``Commission'') is submitting to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) this request for revision of the proposed collection of information. Section 4(g)(8) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act), 15 U.S.C. 78d(g)(8) requires the SEC Ombuds to (i) act as a liaison between the Commission and any retail investor in resolving problems that retail investors may have with the Commission or with self-regulatory organizations (``SROs''); (ii) review and make recommendations regarding policies and procedures to encourage persons to present questions to the Investor Advocate regarding compliance with the securities laws; and (iii) establish safeguards to maintain the confidentiality of communications between the persons described in clause (ii) and the Ombuds. In addition, Section 4(g)(8) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act), 15 U.S.C. 78d(g)(8) requires the Ombuds to submit a semi-annual report to the Investor Advocate describing the activities and evaluating the effectiveness of the Ombuds during the preceding year. Each year, the Commission's Office of the Investor Advocate, Office of the Ombuds (``Ombuds'') receives over 2,500 contacts from investors who have complaints or questions about the SEC or any of the self- regulatory organizations that it oversees. To make it easier for the public to contact the Ombuds, the Ombuds created an electronic form (Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form) that provides drop down options to choose from in order to categorize the investor's complaint or question, and may also provide the investor with automated information about their issue. The Ombudsman Matter Management System (OMMS) Submission Form asks investors to provide information concerning, among other things, their names, how they can be reached, the names of the individuals or entities involved, the nature of their complaint or tip, what documents they can provide, and what, if any, actions they have taken. Use of the OMMS Submission Form is voluntary. Absent the forms, the public still has several ways to contact the Ombuds, including telephone, letters, and email. Investors can access the OMMS Submission Form through the Ombuds web page at the web address https://www.sec.gov/ombuds or directly at the web address https://omms.sec.gov. The dual purpose of the OMMS Submission Form is to make it easier for the public to contact the agency with complaints, questions, tips, or other feedback and to streamline the workflow of Ombuds staff that record, process, and respond to investor contacts. Investors who submit complaints, ask questions, or provide tips do so voluntarily. Although the OMMS Submission Form provides a structured format for incoming investor correspondence, the Commission does not require that investors use any particular form or format when contacting the Ombuds. Investors who choose not to use the OMMS Submission Form will receive the same level of service as those who do. The Ombuds receives approximately 1,500 contacts each year through the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form. The Ombudsman uses the information that investors supply on the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form to review and process the contact (which may, in turn, involve responding to questions, processing complaints, or, as appropriate, referring matters to enforcement or examinations for potential investigations), to maintain a record of contacts, to track the volume of investor complaints, and to analyze trends. This proposed collection is a revision of the previously approved collection for OMMS. The OMMS Submission Form is being revised to include a new information type. Specifically, the user of the revised OMMS Submission Form will be asked to respond to a prepopulated list, which asks whether the submitter is a: Individual Investor; Registered Representative; Accountant; Other Financial Professional; Issuer/ Attorney for an Issuer; Brokerage Firm Compliance Officer; Academic/ Researcher/Student; Member of the Press. The staff of the Commission estimates that the total reporting burden for using the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form is 750 hours. The calculation of this estimate depends on the number of investors who use the forms each year and the estimated time it takes to complete the forms: 1,500 respondents x 30 minutes = 750 burden hours. An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB Control Number. The public may view and comment on this information collection request at: https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAViewICR?ref_nbr=202608-3235-007 or email comment to [email protected] within 30 days of the day after publication of this notice, by December 18, 2026. 1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Rules to permit the listing of binary options overlying KPIs reported by certain issuers of stock (``binary KPI options''). The Exchange's proposal is substantively identical to the recent approval received by Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe) to permit listing of binary options that overlie KPIs. Similar to the approved proposal by Cboe, the Exchange proposes to adopt Section 9 (Binary KPI Options) to describe binary KPI options. The Rules in proposed Section 9 apply only to binary KPI options. All other Rules apply to the trading of binary KPI options, except as otherwise provided or the context otherwise requires. The Exchange proposes to establish these terms in new Rule 5.96-O and additional provisions in proposed 5.98-O, as described below. The Exchange proposes to define a ``binary KPI option'' in new Rule 5.96-O(b) as a cash-settled option contract listed on an underlying KPI of an issuer with an exercise settlement amount that is established at the creation of the option and with a settlement value that is determined by whether a specific KPI disclosed by the issuer in an earnings-related filing submitted to the Commission meets or exceeds its exercise price. The Exchange proposes to define a ``call binary KPI option'' as an option contract that returns an exercise settlement amount if the settlement value of the underlying KPI is at or above the exercise price at expiration (i.e., in- or at-the-money). The term ``Clearing Corporation'' would mean the registered clearing agency designated by the Exchange to clear binary KPI options. The Exchange proposes to define ``exercise price'' (also referred to as ``strike price'') as the value to which the settlement value of the underlying KPI is compared to the exercise settlement amount. For binary KPI options, the exercise price is the exercise threshold of an option contract that establishes a number, value, or measure that is compared against the settlement value of the underlying KPI to determine if the cash payout amount (i.e., the exercise settlement amount) will be paid out. In other words, binary options will have a threshold number as the exercise price that will be used to determine if the exercise criteria of the binary option has been met and the option will be exercised (and if holders will receive the cash payout amount). For binary KPI options, the exercise threshold will be a number that reflects or is compared to the underlying KPI of the binary option. Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change for Transaction Submission Amendments

1. Purpose The primary purpose of the proposed rule change is to enhance the alignment of CMESC's transaction submission process with existing market structures and participant expectations. In particular, the proposed rule change is designed to (i) define single-dealer execution platforms and clarify their role in submitting Eligible Securities Transactions for clearance and settlement; (ii) establish terms for asset managers to submit Eligible Securities Transactions, including block transactions, on behalf of Participants; (iii) update existing descriptions regarding the submission requirements for single-sided and matched transactions; and (iv) make other appropriate clarifying and conforming edits. Definitions The proposed rule change amends Rule 101 to introduce a defined term for Single-Dealer Execution Platforms (``SDEPs''). Specifically, a SDEP would be defined to mean ``a principal-based trade execution platform on which a Participant acts as a dealer on both sides of the market and is counterparty to all transactions occurring on the platform and which is approved by the Corporation to send Eligible Securities Transactions executed on the platform between the single dealer Participant and another Participant to the Corporation for clearance and settlement.'' The existing Rules include references to SDEPs without utilizing a formally defined term. Defining SDEP in the Rulebook will clarify the Rules and align them with terms to be used in certain agreements that will govern operational connections and trade submissions to CMESC. For increased clarity in the Rules and related agreements, Rule 101 would also be amended to introduce the new defined term ``Approved Platforms,'' which would include both SDEPs and Eligible Platforms (the latter of which is already an existing defined term in the Rules). The proposed rule change also amends Rule 101 to introduce a defined term for ``Asset Managers.'' Specifically, an Asset Manager would be defined to mean ``an investment adviser for a Participant that is duly authorized to execute transactions for and submit Eligible Securities Transactions to the Corporation for clearance and settlement in the name, and on behalf, of the Participant.'' The definition is intended to cover a range of potential relationships, including investment managers acting for managed accounts, fund managers acting for funds. An Asset Manager does not have to be a Member or a User, but it is possible that a Member could be acting in the capacity of an Asset Manager for another Participant. This approach aligns with CMESC's overall intention to allow duly authorized third parties (i.e., ``agents'') to perform operational tasks on behalf of principals (i.e., Participants), particularly in the context of managed accounts and funds that would generally rely on a manager for trade execution and submission for clearance and settlement, while the Participants remain primarily liable to CMESC for the underlying obligations. The RMF is being updated to address authorized agents performing operational tasks on behalf of Participants, as well as to clarify the use of the term ``Asset Manager'' in the document. The proposed rule change also amends Rule 101 to introduce a defined term for ``Block Transaction.'' A Block Transaction would be defined to mean ``an Eligible Securities Transaction executed by an Asset Manager as a single transaction on behalf of more than one Participant with a single other Participant as contra-party that is submitted by the Asset Manager to the Corporation for clearance and settlement, where the transaction, if accepted by the Corporation, will be broken into its component transactions and allocated to each Participant on the blocked side of the transaction upon novation by the Corporation.'' The new definition is intended to allow Asset Managers to submit for clearance and settlement a Block Transaction executed on behalf of multiple Participants it manages, including funds, consistent with current market practice. Following novation, the Block Transaction components would be allocated to the accounts of the individual Participants covered by the Block Transaction. Transaction Submission Process The proposed rule change amends Rule 1502 to make a number of related changes to the rules describing the transaction submission process. First, the proposed changes would clarify that SDEPs may be involved in the transaction submission process pursuant to the Rules in the same way as Eligible Platforms, by replacing ``Eligible Platform'' with the proposed new definition ``Approved Platform'' in Rule 1502(a)(i)(A) and (b)(iv), which applies to both Eligible Platforms and SDEPs. Second, the proposed changes would clarify a Member's role in submitting transactions and address Asset Managers' role in submitting transactions, including Block Transactions, to CMESC on behalf of Participants. Specifically, the proposed changes to Rule 1502(a)(i)(A)(x) would permit a duly authorized Member or an Asset Manager to submit a matched Repo Transactions or Cash Treasury Transactions for the respective accounts of two Participants where it has the authority to submit both sides. The proposed changes to Rule 1502(a)(i)(A)(y) would permit a Participant itself, its authorizing Member (if the Participant is a User) or its Asset Manager to submit a single-sided Repo Transaction or Cash Treasury Transaction for the account of the Participant, and further clarifying that where an Asset Manager submits such a single-sided transaction for the account of a Participant that is deemed submission by the Participant. The proposed changes to Rule 1502(a)(i)(A)(z) would enable an Asset Manager to submit an alleged Repo Transaction or Cash Treasury Transaction for the Account of a Participant, which is deemed submission by the Participant. Lastly, additional proposed changes throughout Rule 1502(a)(i)(A) update the in-line explanations of certain terms to account for an Asset Manager ac

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule, effective November 1, 2026. SPXO Electronic Execution Surcharge and Other Conforming Changes First, the Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule to apply the SPX/SPXW Electronic Execution Surcharge to SPXO options. The Exchange intends to list SPX options that are a.m.-settled under the OSI root symbol SPXO beginning on November 9, 2026. Currently, the Fees Schedule assesses an Electronic Execution Surcharge of $0.14 per contract on electronic executions in SPXW options (noting that this is different than the Electronic Execution Surcharge of $0.21 for SPX). The Exchange proposes to amend the Fees Schedule to provide that the $0.14 per contract surcharge will also apply to electronic executions in SPXO options. In addition, the Exchange proposes to add SPXO to each other provision of the Fees Schedule that currently references SPXW (e.g., by amending references to ``SPX (incl SPXW)'' to read ``SPX (incl SPXW and SPXO),'' and references to ``SPX/SPXW'' to read ``SPX/SPXW/SPXO''), including in the Underlying Symbol List A rate table, the Index License Surcharge, the Floor Broker Solicitation Surcharge, the SPX/SPXW/SPXO Liquidity Provider Sliding Scale, the SCORe Program, the Market-Maker Tier Appointment Fees, the Floor Broker Trading Surcharge, the Floor Brokerage Fees and Floor Brokerage Fees Discount Scale, the GTH1 and GTH2 SPX/SPXW/SPXO LMM Incentive Programs, and footnote 41, so that SPXO is treated in the same manner as SPXW throughout the Fees Schedule. The Exchange intends to launch SPXO options on November 9, 2026. Accordingly, no SPXO fees will be assessed prior to the launch date. The Exchange believes that SPXO options are comparable to SPXW options, as both are weekly options on the S&P 500 Index exclusively listed on the Exchange (the primary difference is that SPXO options are a.m.-settled while SPXW options are p.m.-settled), and that it is therefore appropriate to assess the same Electronic Execution Surcharge on electronic executions in both products. QCC Fees, Initiating Credits, and Credit Cap Next, the Exchange proposes to amend the fees, credits, and credit cap applicable to QCC orders. Currently, the Exchange assesses a fee of $0.18 per contract on Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer QCC orders (fee code QN), and a fee of $0.00 per contract on Customer and Professional Customer QCC orders. The Exchange proposes to increase the fee for Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer QCC orders from $0.18 to $0.20 per contract. Fees for Customer and Professional Customer QCC orders will remain unchanged. The Exchange also currently provides a credit of $0.11 per contract to the initiating side of a QCC transaction, except that no credit is paid on Customer (C) to Customer (C) executions, Customer (C) to Professional (U) executions, Professional (U) to Professional (U) executions or Professional (U) to Customer (C). The Exchange proposes to amend the initiating credit so that the amount of the credit depends on (i) the initiating side and (ii) the contra side. Specifically, as proposed, the initiator of a QCC transaction will receive (i) no credit where both the initiating and contra sides are Customer or Professional Customer orders (in accordance with current practice); (ii) a credit for the initiating order of $0.18 per contract where only one side of the transaction is a Non-Customer, Non- Professional Customer order; and (iii) a credit for the initiating order of $0.30 per contract where both sides of the transaction are Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer orders. To reflect this structure, the Exchange proposes to bifurcate the Per Contract Credit column of the QCC Rate Table into two sections, one for Customer and Professional (capacity codes C and U) and one for all other capacities, mirroring the existing fee structure, and to set forth the applicable credits for each. Because the exclusion of Customer-to-Customer, Customer-to-Professional, and Professional-to-Professional executions will be reflected in the proposed credit amounts themselves, the Exchange also proposes to delete the existing sentence in the QCC Rate Table Notes providing that credits will not be paid on such executions. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Order Instituting Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Order Instituting Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual

I. Introduction On July 31, 2026, New York Stock Exchange LLC (``NYSE'' or the ``Exchange'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to amend Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual (``Manual'') to extend the transition period in which a listed company must establish and internal audit function. The proposed rule change was published for comment in the Federal Register on August 18, 2026. On September 25, 2026, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act, the Commission designated a longer period within which to take action on the proposed rule change. The Commission is instituting proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. II. Description of the Proposed Rule Change Section 303A.07(c) of the Manual states that each company listed on the Exchange must have an internal audit function. The Exchange states that the purpose of the internal audit function is to provide an issuer's management and audit committee with ongoing assessments of the issuer's risk management processes and system of internal controls. The function may be outsourced to a third-party service provider other than an issuer's independent auditor. Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the Manual provide a transition period for certain issuers to become compliant with the internal audit function. Pursuant to Section 303A.07, issuers must have an internal audit function in place no later than the first anniversary of their listing date. The Exchange proposes to extend the transition period to implement an internal audit function from one year to five years. According to the Exchange, issuers have expressed concern that developing a capable internal audit function within the first year of listing presents challenges as issuers adjust to life as a newly public company. In expressing concern over the current one-year compliance period, issuers often cite competing business and regulatory obligations requiring management's attention and the challenges of building an internal audit function to assess a company's internal control environment while a company is still in its early stages and continuing to grow. The Exchange states that it believes that having a robust internal audit function is a key component of sound corporate governance, but agrees that providing issuers with additional time to develop such function will result in a more effective function. The Exchange further states that, during the proposed five-year transition period, other requirements will continue to provide sufficient assurance that issuers listed on the Exchange are appropriately managing risk. All issuers listed on the Exchange are required to have an Audit Committee comprised of at least three independent directors. The Audit Committee of an issuer listed on the Exchange must have a written charter that requires it to ``at least annually, obtain and review a report by the [company's] independent auditor describing: the firm's internal quality-control procedures; any material issues raised by the most recent internal quality-control review.'' In addition, Section 404(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act obligates management to maintain an adequate internal control structure for financial reporting and annually assess its effectiveness. Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act requires a company's independent auditor to provide an attestation on management's internal control assessment. In addition, the CEO and CFO certifications required by Sections 302 and 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act require an additional level of management responsibility for internal control oversight. The Exchange states that the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and its provisions discussed herein was enacted after the Exchange first adopted its internal audit requirement and that, in this regard, the internal audit function may be viewed as a supplement for the statutory protections embodied in the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. The Exchange also states that Nasdaq Stock Market (``Nasdaq'') does not require companies listed on that exchange to maintain an internal audit function. III. Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove SR- NYSEAMER-2026-17 and Grounds for Disapproval Under Consideration The Commission is instituting proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved. Institution of such proceedings is appropriate at this time in view of the legal and policy issues raised by the proposed rule change. Institution of proceedings does not indicate that the Commission has reached any conclusions with respect to any of the issues involved. Rather, as described below, the Commission seeks and encourages interested persons to provide additional comment on the proposed rule change to inform the Commission's analysis of whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. Pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act, the Commission is providing notice of the grounds for disapproval under consideration. The Commission is instituting proceedings to allow for additional analysis of, and input from commenters with respect to, the proposed rule change's consistency with the Act, and in particular, Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, which requires, among other things, that the rules of a national securities exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. As discussed above, the Exchange's proposal would extend the transition period

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Provide Transparency to the Process for Selection of an Initial Trading Date
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Provide Transparency to the Process for Selection of an Initial Trading Date

1. Purpose Nasdaq proposes to adopt new Listing Rule 5205(j), which will specify that, once a company's application to list a security is approved, the security will begin trading on Nasdaq on a date and at a time that is mutually agreed upon by Nasdaq and the company. Nasdaq believes that including this requirement in its rules will add transparency to Nasdaq's process of scheduling initial public offerings and other new listings. After a security has been approved for listing, Nasdaq works with the issuing company and its advisors to schedule a preferred initial trading date, which may in unusual circumstances be moved by either Nasdaq or the company due to market conditions, company preference or other events where launch is not in the interests of investors or the market. In the case of an initial listing that uses the Nasdaq IPO Halt Cross to initiate trading, Nasdaq will also establish, in conjunction with the company and its underwriter or financial advisor (as applicable), a time to commence the ``Pre-Launch Period.'' No date or time would ever be selected without the agreement of the company, and the Exchange expects that companies will coordinate with their underwriter or financial advisors, as applicable, when selecting the date and time. While this has been Nasdaq's longstanding practice, and confusion has not previously occurred, Nasdaq believes it will aid transparency to modify its rules to explicitly state that trading will begin on a date, and at a time, that is mutually agreed upon by Nasdaq and the listing company. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest, by adding transparency to how the date and time for the initiation of trading is selected. Further, requiring the mutual agreement of Nasdaq and the company will enhance investor protection in rare instances where market conditions, company preference or other events make the selection of a certain day or time suboptimal. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change merely reflects how Nasdaq, together with the listing company, determines the trading date for new securities and will not have any burden on competition. C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others No written comments were either solicited or received. III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder. Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder. A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii), the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing. The Exchange states that the proposed change provides transparency to Nasdaq's current practice of establishing the day and time for a security to initially trade and would codify this practice, making no change to how listings are scheduled. The Exchange further states that waiving the operative delay will eliminate any potential confusion as to the mechanism for selecting a date and time during that delayed period. For these reasons, and because the proposed rule change raises no new or novel legal or regulatory issues, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Therefore, the Commission waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change operative upon filing. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved. IV. Solicitation of Comments Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule To Lower Certain Initiating Participant Rebates in Customer Best Execution Auctions
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule To Lower Certain Initiating Participant Rebates in Customer Best Execution Auctions

1. Purpose The purpose of this filing is to lower certain initiating participant rebates related to CUBE Auctions. The Exchange proposes to implement the fee change effective November 2, 2026. Background The Exchange has established various pricing incentives designed to encourage increased electronic volume executed on the Exchange, including, but not limited to, the American Customer Engagement (``ACE'') Program. To encourage participation in the ACE Program and CUBE Auctions, the Exchange offers an ACE Initiating Participant Rebate to ACE Program participants that initiate Single-Leg CUBE Auctions, Complex CUBE Auctions, and AON Single-Leg or AON Complex CUBE Auctions. Currently, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for each of these auctions $0.115 per contact for all issues (i.e., penny and non-penny). In addition, the Exchange offers the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate that enables non-ACE Program participants to qualify for this Rebate on certain initiating Complex CUBE Auctions provided they meet certain monthly volume qualification levels and increase their initiating CUBE volume. Currently, the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate is $0.115 per contract for all issues. The Exchange proposes to reduce the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for all three auctions and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate, for Complex CUBE Auctions, from $0.115 per contract to $0.105 per contract across all issues. The proposed change is the result of the Exchange's ongoing reassessment and rebalancing of its fee structure overall and, in this instance, its CUBE rebate structure. The proposal only slightly reduces the amount of the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate where applicable. As such, the Exchange believes that the Rebates will continue to encourage ATP Holders to initiate CUBE Auctions, whether single-leg, complex, or AON. The change will apply equally to all similarly situated market participants. Moreover, the Exchange believes all market participants stand to benefit from the continuing increased order flow, which promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery. Increased order flow promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery, which enhances market quality for all participants. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and (5) of the Act, in particular, because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members, issuers and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers. As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for options securities transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system ``has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.'' There are currently 20 registered options exchanges competing for order flow. Based on publicly available information and, excluding index-based options, no single exchange has more than 16% of the market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options trades. Therefore, currently no exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. More specifically, in September 2026, the Exchange had 12.39% market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. In such a low concentrated and highly competitive market, no single options exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of option order flow. In response to these competitive forces and as discussed herein, the Exchange has established various pricing incentives regarding its CUBE Auctions, including, but not limited to, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate, the Alternative Initiating Rebate and Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate, which are designed to encourage ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auction and to direct (increased) volume to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed changes in the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebate are reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory and will continue to provide the intended incentive for ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auctions on the Exchange. To the extent this purpose is achieved, the Exchange believes that the proposed CUBE rebate would not discourage ATP Holders from directing activity to the Exchange. The Exchange also believes that the proposal represents an equitable allocation of credits and is not unfairly discriminatory because the proposal will apply equally to all similarly situated ATP Holders. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition In accordance with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change would impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Intramarket Competition. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 5.7 and 5.31(b)(1) and (c) for the Queuing Period, Order and Quote Entry, and Opening Auction Times Regarding the Global Trading Hours (“GTH”) Sessions
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 5.7 and 5.31(b)(1) and (c) for the Queuing Period, Order and Quote Entry, and Opening Auction Times Regarding the Global Trading Hours (“GTH”) Sessions

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rules 5.7 and 5.31(b)(1) and (c) to permit the Queuing Period and order and quote entry on C2 to begin earlier than they do today. The proposed rule change is substantively identical to the changes Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe Options'') recently made to the Queuing Period, order and quote entry, and opening auction update dissemination times in Cboe Options Rules 5.7(a), 5.31(b)(1), and 5.31(c) for option classes other than index options eligible for Global Trading Hours (``GTH''). Background C2 offers Global Trading Hours (``GTH'') for certain index options (currently, DJX options) from 8:30 a.m. to 9:15 a.m. Under current Rule 5.31(b)(1), the Queuing Period begins at 7:30 a.m. for all classes, including both RTH Only classes and classes eligible for GTH. The Queuing Period is the time period prior to the initiation of an opening rotation during which the System accepts orders and quotes in the Queuing Book for participation in the opening rotation for the applicable trading session. Under current Rule 5.31(b)(1), the Queuing Period begins at 7:30 a.m. Eastern Time for all classes. Consistent with that time, current Rule 5.7 provides that Users can enter orders into the System from 7:30 a.m. until market close, and cancel previously entered orders. Under current Rule 5.31(c), the Exchange disseminates opening auction updates for a series beginning at a time (determined by the Exchange) no earlier than one hour prior to the expected initiation of the opening rotation for a trading session and until the conclusion of the opening rotation for a series. Pre-Opening Queuing Period Start Time The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 5.31(b)(1) to provide that the Queuing Period for Opening Auctions begins at such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., for all classes. Moving the start of the Queuing Period to no earlier than 6:00 a.m. allows the Exchange to lengthen the pre-opening Queuing Period, affording market participants additional time to enter, modify, and cancel orders and quotes for participation in the opening rotation and promoting a smoother, more orderly opening. This change is administrative and ministerial in nature. It adjusts only the time window during which orders and quotes are accepted for the Queuing Book and does not alter trading mechanics, order priority, execution logic, or price formation. Participants are not required to submit orders earlier; the extended window simply provides additional flexibility for those who choose to use it. This change affects only when orders and quotes are accepted for the Queuing Book, not when trading begins; the opening rotation times remain unchanged. The Exchange's approach provides for a start time determined by Exchange notice rather than a fixed time, affording the Exchange operational flexibility. For consistency, the Exchange also proposes to amend the opening auction update dissemination time in Rule 5.31(c) to begin at such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., so that the Exchange may begin disseminating opening auction updates at the start of the Queuing Period (and thus incorporate orders and quotes submitted during the entire Queuing Period in those updates). The Exchange also proposes to amend Rule 5.7 to update the order and quote entry time to conform to the proposed Queuing Period change in Rule 5.31(b)(1). As amended, Rule 5.7 will provide that Users can enter orders into the System from such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., until market close, and cancel previously entered orders. These changes ensure that Users can begin entering orders and quotes at the same time the System begins accepting orders and quotes into the Queuing Book. Because Rule 5.33(c)(1) provides that the System accepts complex orders for inclusion in the COB Opening Process at the times and in the manner set forth in Rule 5.31, the proposed change to the Queuing Period start time will also apply to the entry of complex orders for the COB Opening Process. These changes are administrative in nature. The Queuing Period concept already exists, and the opening auction update dissemination process is unchanged in substance. The change raises no novel policy questions. It merely expands an existing administrative preparation window without affecting how orders are prioritized, matched, or executed. The Exchange notes that while NYSE American LLC's (``NYSE American'') extended trading hours framework provides for a fixed 6:00 a.m. order acceptance time rather than a time determined by Exchange notice, the Exchange believes its discretionary approach is appropriate. The rule merely sets a floor (``no earlier than 6:00 a.m.''); it does not mandate the Exchange to begin queuing at that time. All Exchange determinations regarding the time at which the Queuing Period will begin will be announced via Exchange Notice, so market participants will have advance notice and transparency regarding the applicable start time. In addition, the Exchange believes providing the Exchange with discretion affords operational flexibility to adjust the start time in response to feedback from market participants and evolving market conditions, which benefits investors by allowing the Exchange to optimize the preparation window based on actual market participant needs. The proposed rule change does not amend the operation of the Queuing Period following a trading halt pursuant to Rule 5.31(g), and does not change any other aspect of the opening auction process. 1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to eliminate the requirement in Rule 14.001(b)(1) that the Exchange distribute an information circular to Members prior to the commencement of trading in each UTP Exchange Traded Product. The information circular generally includes the same information as contained in the information circular provided by the listing exchange. The Exchange also proposes to add express cross- references to Rules 3.007 and 3.021 in Rule 14.001(a), amend the written description provision in Rule 14.001(b)(2)(B), and make conforming renumbering changes. Rule 14.001(b) governs the trading of UTP Exchange Traded Products on the Exchange. UTP Exchange Traded Products are derivative securities products listed on another national securities exchange that trade on the Exchange pursuant to unlisted trading privileges (``UTP''). Under current Rule 14.001(b)(1), the Exchange must distribute an information circular prior to the commencement of trading in each UTP Exchange Traded Product that generally mirrors the information circular provided by the listing exchange, including: (a) the special risks of trading the UTP Exchange Traded Product; (b) the Exchange Rules that will apply to the product, including Rule 3.007; (c) information about the dissemination of the value of the underlying assets or indices; and (d) the applicable trading hours for the UTP Exchange Traded Product and the risks of trading during the period from 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and from 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. due to the lack of calculation or dissemination of the underlying index value, the IIV or a similar value. The Exchange proposes to delete Rule 14.001(b)(1) in its entirety. The product-specific information circular requirement is unnecessary because the primary listing exchange's information circular already provides Members with the same disclosures the Exchange would otherwise be required to reproduce. Members have access to the primary listing exchange's information circular prior to the commencement of UTP trading and may rely upon it for the same purposes. Requiring the Exchange to prepare and distribute a separate circular containing duplicative information serves no independent investor-protection function. The Exchange also proposes to amend Rule 14.001(a) to add express cross-references to Rule 3.007 (Recommendations to Customers) and Rule 3.021 (Customer Disclosures). These rules already apply to Members by operation of the Exchange's rulebook. The cross-references are intended to preserve the visibility of the applicable customer-protection framework in the context of UTP Exchange Traded Products after deletion of Rule 14.001(b)(1). Rule 3.007 independently requires a Member recommending a UTP Exchange Traded Product to have reasonable grounds for believing the recommendation is suitable for the customer based on the facts disclosed by the customer after reasonable inquiry into the customer's other securities holdings, financial situation, and needs. Similarly, Rule 3.021 independently requires Members to disclose the material risks of extended-hours trading before accepting a customer order for execution in the Pre-Market or Post-Market Session. These standing obligations are not contingent on the Exchange's issuance of a product-specific circular. Because Rule 14.001(b)(1) has historically served as the mechanism through which the Exchange informs Members of the application of the written-description provisions in Rule 14.001(b)(2)(B), the Exchange proposes a conforming amendment to that paragraph. The Exchange will continue to inform Members of the application of the written- description provisions by information circular, but proposes to require that any written description referenced therein be provided in a form approved by the listing exchange, rather than the Exchange, or prepared by the open-ended management company issuing the securities. The Exchange will notify Members by information circular that such written description will only be required when mandated by the listing exchange. This amendment is consistent with the broader purpose of the proposed rule change: where the listing exchange's information circular already provides Members with the information necessary to assess a UTP Exchange Traded Product, a duplicative written description obligation serves no independent investor protection function. Members may rely on the listing exchange's information circular in the same manner and to the same effect. The Exchange also proposes to renumber existing Rules 14.001(b)(2) through (6) as Rules 14.001(b)(1) through (5), respectively. Finally, the Exchange proposes to delete the reference to subparagraph (2) in current Rule 14.001(b)(2) (as proposed to be re- numbered to Rule 14.001(b)(1) herein) such that instead of reading ``this subparagraph (2) apply only to'' it would read ``this subparagraph apply only to.'' The proposal is based on and substantially similar to the Cboe BZX proposal and the subsequent MIAX Pearl, IEX, and MEMX proposals. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and specifically with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5), in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange also believes the proposal is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b)(5) that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. 1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Section A (Transaction Fees) and Section F (Lead Market Maker Program) of the TXSE Fee Schedule to: (i) increase the rebate provided for orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (ii) increase the fee for orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (iii) reduce the fee for orders that add or remove non- displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00; (iv) introduce an enhanced rebate designed to incentivize displayed liquidity in TXSE- listed corporate securities; and (v) amend certain definitions and add notes to the Lead Market Maker Program. The Exchange proposes to implement these changes effective on November 2, 2026. The Exchange's Fee Schedule sets forth the standard rebates and fees applied per share for orders that add and remove liquidity, respectively. Currently, TXSE provides a rebate of $0.0031 per share for orders priced at or above $1.00 that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee of $0.0030 per share for orders that remove displayed liquidity from the Exchange. For securities priced below $1.00, the Exchange provides a rebate of 0.15% of total dollar value (``TDV'') for orders that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee of 0.15% of TDV for orders that remove displayed liquidity from the Exchange. The Exchange currently charges a fee of $0.0002 per share for orders that add non-displayed liquidity to the Exchange or remove non-displayed liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange currently charges a fee of 0.05% of TDV for orders that add non-displayed liquidity to the Exchange or remove non-displayed liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced below $1.00. Base Rates The Exchange now proposes to amend its base rates applicable to orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00. The proposed rebate for orders that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange is $0.0032 per share, an increase of $0.0001 from the current rate of $0.0031 per share. In addition, the Exchange proposes to amend its base rates applicable to orders that add or remove non- displayed liquidity in both securities priced at or above $1.00 and securities priced below $1.00. For orders that add or remove non- displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00, the Exchange proposes to charge a fee of $0.0006, an increase of $0.0004 from its current rate of $0.0002 per share. For orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00, the Exchange proposes to make these executions free. The purpose of revising the rates associated with adding and removing displayed and non-displayed liquidity is for business and competitive reasons, as the proposed change is intended to incentivize Members to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange by providing a higher rebate for displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange and charging a higher fee for non-displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange or remove liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange notes that its proposed base rebate for orders that add liquidity to the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00 would remain significantly higher than the base rebates provided by competitors for orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange notes that its proposed fee for orders that add non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00 is similar to at least one competitor. The Exchange's proposed fee for orders that remove non- displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00 would remain lower than the fees assessed by competitors for orders that remove non- displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange's proposal to make executions free in all non-displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange in securities priced below $1.00 aligns with the pricing that competitors offer for similar executions. In addition, the Exchange's proposal to make executions free in all orders that remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00 differs from competitors in that many competitors assess a fee for non-displayed orders that remove liquidity. In totality, the Exchange believes its proposed fee structure is appropriate in furthering its goal of encouraging Members to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange as it provides a competitive rebate to Members who add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee to those Members who either remove displayed liquidity in all securities or who add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00. Displayed Liquidity Enhanced Rebate The Exchange next proposes to introduce an enhanced rebate designed to incentivize quoting in TXSE-listed corporate securities. The Exchange proposes to provide an enhanced rebate of $0.0038 per share in securities priced at or above $1.00 to Members that add displayed liquidity in a TXSE-listed corporate security. The enhanced rebate would not apply to securities priced below $1.00. The proposed enhanced rebate is designed to encourage Members to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange in TXSE-listed corporate securities, which contributes to a deeper, more liquid market and provides additional execution opportunities for active market participants. By offering enhanced rebate opportunities to incentivize increased liquidity provision, the Exchange seeks to encourage greater trading activity and additional execution opportunities for Members, thereby promoting more robust price discovery and improving overall market quality for all market participants. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend General 4, Rule 1240 To Adopt a New Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program
