Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend General 4, Rule 1240 To Adopt a New Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program

1. Purpose The purpose of the proposed rule change is to amend General 4, Rule 1240 (Continuing Education) to adopt new Supplementary Material .03 (Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program) and to make a conforming amendment to General 4, Rule 1240(a)(6) (Delivery of the Regulatory Element) to conform the Exchange's continuing education requirements to recent changes made by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (``FINRA'') to FINRA Rule 1240. Pursuant to General 4, Rule 1240, registered persons of Exchange members are required to complete continuing education (``CE'') that consists of two mandatory programs, a Regulatory Element and a Firm Element. Regulatory Element CE, which is administered by FINRA, focuses on regulatory requirements and industry standards. Firm Element CE is provided by each member to its registered persons and focuses on the member's securities products, services, and strategies, its policies, and industry trends. The Exchange's Rule 1240 is identical to FINRA Rule 1240, and the Exchange periodically amends its rule to remain harmonized with FINRA's rule. FINRA has represented that it received a variety of suggestions from member firms and industry groups regarding changes to the Regulatory Element CE requirement for senior leaders (e.g., chief executive officer, chief financial officer), including in response to FINRA Regulatory Notice 25-07. The Exchange agrees with FINRA that Regulatory Element CE provides individuals with valuable training on recent developments in regulatory requirements and industry standards and, as such, is appropriate for all registered persons, including senior leaders. Senior leaders, however, may realize greater benefit from Regulatory Element CE training that draws from the annual Regulatory Element content but is tailored to their unique roles at a member. Senior leaders may engage with applicable rules differently than frontline representatives and principals because they have broader visibility and responsibilities across their member firm, and, often, its broader organizational structure. Regulatory Element CE content for such leaders therefore may be more effective if it covers the information addressed in the various Regulatory Element CE learning plans but presents the information from a broader, firm-wide perspective, such as firm risks, control systems, approaches to pressure-test firm capabilities and vulnerabilities, and similar enterprise-level considerations. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .03 to General 4, Rule 1240 to establish a Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program (``Interim Program'') identical to that adopted and administered by FINRA. A member may elect to have a covered person who is a senior leader satisfy the requirement to complete the Regulatory Element by participating in the Interim Program. For purposes of the Interim Program, the term ``senior leader'' means any covered person listed on a member's Schedule A of Form BD; any other covered person serving on a member's executive, management or operations committees; or any covered person with similar status or functions who is employed at an affiliate of a member. Participating senior leaders would continue to be required to take Regulatory Element CE on an annual basis, but the content of the training and the method of delivery would be different. The Interim Program would be administered in a manner prescribed by FINRA and as set forth in the FINRA Filing, for a period starting on November 2, 2026, and ending on December 31, 2028. The Regulatory Element material for participating covered persons would be developed by FINRA and based on the roles and responsibilities of senior leaders. As described in the FINRA Filing, FINRA would consider the annual learning plan topics assigned to each registration category, but, rather than limiting the content to the specific registration categories the senior leaders hold, the materials would cover content across all registration categories and present significant rule changes, key regulatory developments, and other Regulatory Element topics from the unique organizational vantage point of senior leaders. The materials would remain consistent with the core objectives of Regulatory Element CE. Under the Interim Program, the chief compliance officer (``CCO'') or other senior compliance officer at a participating member would provide the training to participating senior leaders (including any participating senior leaders of affiliated entities), and would have the discretion to supplement the training materials to provide the most relevant and effective training for the member's senior leaders. The CCO of a member designated under General 9, Section 21(c) would provide FINRA with the list of participating senior leaders and represent to FINRA that the senior leaders completed the Regulatory Element material in a manner prescribed by FINRA. Further, a senior leader who participates in the Interim Program would certify that he or she has completed the Regulatory Element material, and the member would retain such certification. Senior leaders who participate and successfully complete the training would satisfy their annual Regulatory Element requirement under Rule 1240; those who do not participate would be required to complete the Regulatory Element CE courses assigned by FINRA, as they do today. In connection with the Interim Program, the Exchange also proposes to amend General 4, Rule 1240(a)(6) (Delivery of the Regulatory Element), which currently provides that the Regulatory Element shall be administered through Web-based delivery or such other technological manner and format as specified by the Exchange. The Exchange proposes to delete the word ``technological'' so that the rule would provide that the Regulatory Element shall be administered through Web-based delivery or such other manner and format as specified by the Exchange. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; 24X National Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Warrant Performance Incentive Program

Self-Regulatory Organizations; 24X National Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Warrant Performance Incentive Program

1. Purpose The Exchange adopted a warrant performance incentive program (``Program'') to allow Members of the Exchange who participate in the Program (``Participants'') to earn the right to purchase Non-Voting Common Units of 24X US Holdings LLC (``24X US Holdco''), the Exchange's parent company. As described in the Warrant Program Release, each Member of the Exchange may become a Participant in the Program by prepaying $500,000 in Exchange fees (``Prepayment Fee'') and satisfying the Program eligibility requirements. Upon joining the Program, each Participant will receive a warrant that vests based on the Participant's achievement of certain minimum trading volumes (``Target Volume'') on the Exchange during each designated pre- determined period in which the Program is in effect (``Measurement Period'') and the Exchange's achievement of a minimum market share during such Measurement Periods (``24X Minimum Overall Market Share''). When the warrants vest, Participants will have the right to exercise the warrants to purchase a certain number of 24X US Holdco Non-Voting Common Units. The Exchange has determined to revise the Program to make additional Non-Voting Common Units available to be purchased by Participants starting in the first Measurement Period of 2027 (``Additional Equity''), under different terms than those applicable to the Non-Voting Common Units currently available to be purchased through the Program (``Original Equity''). Specifically, the right to purchase Additional Equity would extend through two additional Measurement Periods in 2028, would be subject to a reduced Prepayment Fee, and would be based on maker volume only instead of total trading volume. The Exchange also proposes to make two additional changes to the terms of the Program that would apply to the right to purchase both the Original Equity and the Additional Equity. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF and the Invesco Galaxy Ethereum ETF
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF and the Invesco Galaxy Ethereum ETF

1. Purpose The Commission has previously approved the listing and trading of shares for the Bitcoin Trust and the ETH Trust under Rule 14.11(e)(4), and each Trust currently lists and trades on the Exchange. The Exchange now proposes to transition the Trusts to operate under the recently Commission-approved generic listing standards for Commodity- Based Trust Shares pursuant to Rule 14.11(e)(4) (``Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4)''). Each Trust will meet the requirements of Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4) and will be required to comply with the continued listing requirements set forth in such Rule. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is designed to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest because it would provide for the transition of the Trusts from being listed pursuant to the Approval Orders to Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4) instead. The proposed change would allow the Shares to continue listing and trading on the Exchange and permit the Trusts to operate in reliance on the generic listing standards in Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4) instead of the terms of the Approval Orders, thereby facilitating the continued listing and trading of exchange-traded products that will enhance competition among market participants, to the benefit of investors and the marketplace. Each Trust will meet the requirements of Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4) and will be required to comply with the continued listing standards set forth in Amended Rule 14.11(e)(4). B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purpose of the Act. As discussed above, the proposed change is intended to facilitate the continued listing and trading of the Fund on the Exchange, thereby promoting competition among exchange-traded products to the benefit of investors and the marketplace. C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change. III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder. Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; or (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder. A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii), the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing. The Commission believes that waiving the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it will allow the Exchange to implement the proposed rule change without delay, thereby providing for the continued listing and trading of the Trusts' Shares, and does not introduce any novel regulatory issues. Accordingly, the Commission designates the proposed rule change to be operative upon filing. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved. IV. Solicitation of Comments Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods: Electronic Comments Use the Commission's internet comment form (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml); or Send an email to [email protected]. Please include file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-093 on the subject line. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change by The Options Clearing Corporation Concerning the Implementation of a Fee Holiday for the Period Beginning December 1, 2026, and Ending December 31, 2026

1. Purpose Background As the sole clearing agency for standardized equity options listed on national securities exchanges registered with the Commission, and with respect to OCC's clearance and settlement of futures and stock loan transactions, OCC maintains policies and procedures to manage the risks borne by OCC as a central counterparty. One such risk that OCC manages is general business risk, that is, the risk of potential impairment to OCC's financial position resulting from a decline in revenues or an increase in expenses. To manage this risk and help to ensure that OCC can continue operations and services as a going concern if general business losses materialize, OCC has adopted its Capital Management Policy, which provides the framework by which OCC manages its capital. Amending OCC's schedule of fees is one action used by OCC to manage its capital. Pursuant to OCC's rule-filed Capital Management Policy, and as required by Exchange Act rules applicable to OCC, OCC must maintain LNAFBE sufficient to cover at least six months of operating expenses, among other measures (``Target Capital Requirement''). Because OCC is required to maintain such funds, the LNAFBE used to meet the Target Capital Requirement cannot be used to cover operational expenses and any increase in expenses must be covered by current revenue or cash held in excess of the Target Capital Requirement. The Capital Management Plan further sets 110% of the Target Capital Requirement as an early warning threshold. If LNAFBE falls below the early warning threshold, OCC management and Board must discuss whether a fee increase is necessary. In the filing to implement the 2025 fee increase (``2025 Fee Filing''), OCC projected that its LNAFBE would fall below OCC's Target Capital Requirement by the end of Q1 2025 and took action prior to hitting the early warning threshold. At the time, OCC stated it did not believe it would be prudent, given its designation as a SIFMU, to allow its LNAFBE to decline past the early warning threshold prior to taking action to ensure that OCC maintains sufficient LNAFBE to satisfy its regulatory requirements and so that it may continue to operate as a going concern if it were to experience general business losses. However, in the 2025 Fee Filing, OCC emphasized its commitment to aligning its revenues with its costs and capital needs and stated that, consistent with its past practice, if revenues exceed costs and OCC's LNAFBE is above the early warning threshold, OCC would consider utilizing tools to lower the cost of clearing for market participants, as provided under its Capital Management Policy. Later in 2025, OCC followed through and implemented a fee holiday for December 2025 to help lower clearing costs for market participants. Today, OCC is continuing this practice and instituting a fee holiday for December 2026. Proposed Fee Holiday OCC proposes to implement a fee holiday for the month of December 2026. OCC has in place policies and procedures, including the Capital Management Policy, to control costs and regularly review fees and operating expenses, including during its annual budgeting process. Consistent with the Capital Management Policy, OCC set its clearing fees based on factors including OCC's annual budgeted or forecasted operating expenses and projected revenue. However, clearing volume, and therefore revenue, have outpaced projections and OCC currently has LNAFBE in excess of its early warning threshold. In addition to clearing fees, OCC receives revenue from the interest paid on the cash margin collateral it holds with the Federal Reserve System and elsewhere. In October 2026, OCC began paying Clearing Members interest on their margin cash at a rate based on the interest rate OCC receives from the Federal Reserve, less a cash management fee. For budgeting purposes, OCC assumed it would begin paying interest on margin cash in July 2026. Therefore, OCC had three fewer months of interest expenses than anticipated, further contributing to the amount of LNAFBE OCC has in excess of the early warning threshold. The fee holiday will allow OCC to return excess capital to market participants and clearing members while still maintaining sufficient capital to maintain compliance with the Capital Management Policy and regulatory requirements. In evaluating its current LNAFBE and projections for 2027, OCC determined that a fee holiday is warranted for December 2026. Based on recent volumes, OCC estimates that the fee holiday for the month of December will lead to approximately $77 million in lost revenue. Despite this, OCC believes it will remain above the 2026 early warning threshold ($355.3 million) as well as its projected early warning threshold for 2027 ($390.8 million). To make this determination, OCC evaluated revenue and LNAFBE under a wide range of volume scenarios including current average daily volume (``ADV''), 60 million ADV, and - 4% ADV growth. In all scenarios except the negative growth scenario, OCC remained above its early warning threshold through the end of 2027 even with the fee holiday. OCC, however, does not believe the negative growth scenario is realistic, and it would result in ADV decreasing by 50% to 35.5 million contracts a day by the end of 2027. The scenario was selected to illustrate the level of volume decrease that would cause OCC to drop below its early warning threshold. Nonetheless, under this extreme scenario, OCC remained above its early warning threshold through October 2027, meaning OCC would have time to react if the negative ADV growth scenario becomes more realistic. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Sections 1003 and 1009 of the NYSE American Company Guide

I. Introduction On March 6, 2026, NYSE American LLC (``NYSE American'' or the ``Exchange'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'' or ``SEC''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to amend Sections 1003 and 1009 of the NYSE American Company Guide (``Company Guide'') to establish that an issuer must maintain a certain market capitalization in order to remain listed on the Exchange. The proposed rule change was published for comment in the Federal Register on March 20, 2026. On April 29, 2026, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act, the Commission designated a longer period within which to take action on the proposed rule change. On June 2, 2026, the Commission instituted proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. On September 14, 2026, the Commission issued a notice of designation of a longer period of time for Commission action on proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. The Commission received several comment letters, which are addressed below. This order approves the proposed rule change. II. Description of the Proposed Rule Change Section 1003 of the Company Guide sets forth minimum quantitative and qualitative continued listing standards for securities listed on the Exchange. Currently, Section 1003(b)(i) of the Company Guide enumerates circumstances where the Exchange will consider suspension and delisting of a class of common stock because of a sufficiently limited distribution of shares. Section 1003(b)(i) of the Company Guide does not contain a minimum market capitalization requirement. The Exchange states that it has noticed a recent increase in companies that have a very small market capitalization. According to the Exchange, an issuer with a small market capitalization is potentially susceptible to manipulation and more likely to experience trading volatility in its shares because, at smaller sizes, less capital is required to undertake manipulative trading activity. Therefore, the Exchange proposes to amend Section 1003 of the Company Guide to require an issuer to maintain a certain market capitalization in order to remain listed on the Exchange. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to adopt new Section 1003(b)(i)(D) of the Company Guide to specify that if an issuer's class of common stock is determined to have average market capitalization over a consecutive 30 trading-day period of less than $5 million, the Exchange will immediately suspend trading and commence delisting proceedings with respect to such security in accordance with the procedures in Section 1010 of the Company Guide. This order refers to average market capitalization for an issuer's class of common stock over a consecutive 30 trading-day period of $5 million as the ``Minimum Market Capitalization Criteria.'' The Exchange also proposes that an issuer that falls below the Minimum Market Capitalization Criteria would not be eligible to follow the procedures to regain compliance outlined in Section 1009 of the Company Guide. The Exchange further proposes to amend Section 1009 of the Company Guide to add to the list of continued listing standards for which noncompliance does not entitle the issuer to a compliance period a reference to proposed Section 1003(b)(i)(D) of the Company Guide. The Exchange states that all issuers would retain the right to appeal an Exchange delisting decision. The Exchange states that, in its experience, an issuer with a sustained market capitalization below $5 million is likely to be financially distressed and is increasingly susceptible to manipulation due to its small size. The Exchange also states that having a market capitalization below $5 million is frequently a leading indicator that an issuer has other financial concerns that often require a substantial amount of regulatory oversight, and accordingly, the Exchange does not believe that an issuer fitting this profile is appropriate for continued listing on the Exchange. Further, the Exchange states that, in its experience, a company trading at a sustained market capitalization below $5 million is unlikely to regain financial stability and it is therefore appropriate to subject the company to immediate suspension and delisting. The Exchange states that the proposal would become effective immediately upon Commission approval. III. Discussion and Commission Findings The Commission has given careful consideration to the Exchange's proposal and all comments submitted to determine whether the proposal is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations issued thereunder. Under Section 19b(2)(C) of the Act, the Commission must approve the proposed rule change of a self-regulatory organization (``SRO'') if the Commission finds that the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the applicable rules and regulations thereunder; if it does not make such a finding, the Commission must disapprove the proposed rule change. For the reasons discussed herein, the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to national securities exchange. In particular, the Commission finds that the record before the Commission demonstrates that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a national securities exchange. More specifically, the Commission finds that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, which requires, among other things, that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the p

1. Purpose Proposed Chapter 12 of the CDE Rulebook will govern the listing, trading, clearing, adjustment, and settlement of security futures products. Certain rules in proposed Chapter 12 address customer margin requirements for security futures products and are the subject of this filing. The remainder of proposed Chapter 12 is the subject of a separate rule filing under Section 19(b)(7) and Rule 19b-7. CDE Rule 1215 (Customer Margin) is the primary proposed rule establishing customer margin requirements for security futures. CDE Rule 1215 will determine the applicable margin rates, the types of assets that can be accepted by a Participant Firm or Clearing Firm as margin, the effect of an undermargined customer account on Participant Firm and Clearing Firm net capital requirements, and the liquidation requirements for undermargined customer accounts. General Rule. Rule 1215(a) provides that Participant Firms and Clearing Firms that are ``security futures intermediaries'' shall calculate, collect, and maintain the margin required by Rule 1215 and applicable SEC and CFTC regulations. Participant Firms and Clearing Firms that are members of the Clearing House will separately have an obligation to post margin with the Clearing House under the rules of the Clearing House. Rule 1215(f), consistent with Rule 1221(c), clarifies that nothing in Rule 1215 limits the authority of the Clearing House under its own rules with respect to margin collection, settlement processing, default management, or other clearing functions, except as required by law. Margin Rates. Rule 1215(b) provides that the Exchange shall establish initial and maintenance margin requirements applicable to security futures held in a futures account, subject to the minimum margin requirements in SEC Rule 242.403 and CFTC Regulation 41.45. Rule 1215(b) further provides that the margin requirement for a long or short position shall not be less than 15.05%. Rule 1215(b) is substantially identical to CME Rule 930.B.2.c., which provides that ``[t]he Exchange shall establish initial and maintenance performance bond [i.e., margin] requirements applicable to Security Futures and held in a futures account, provided that the performance bond requirement for any long or short position held by a clearing member on behalf of a Customer shall not be less than 15% of the current market value of the relevant Contract; or, such other requirement as may be established by the CFTC and SEC for purposes of CFTC Regulation 41.45(b)(1) and SEC Rule 242.403(b)(1) except as provided below.'' Other exchanges have adopted similar provisions. However, unlike these other exchanges, CDE has set required margin at 15.05%, which is higher than the SEC and CFTC's minimum required margin for security futures positions. CDE added the phrase ``whichever is higher'' to clarify that the minimum margin requirement will be the higher of 15.05% or the amount required by applicable SEC and CFTC regulations. Under SEC and CFTC regulations, Participant Firms and Clearing Firms that are ``security futures intermediaries'' are required to compute and collect required margin based on the ``current market value'' of a security future on a daily basis. Under SEC Rule 242.401(a)(4)(i)(A) and CFTC Regulation 41.43(a)(4)(i)(A), ``current market value'' means on any day, with respect to a single- stock security future, ``the product of the daily settlement price of such security future as shown by any regularly published reporting or quotation service, and the applicable number of shares per contract.'' SEC Rule 242.401(a)(6) and CFTC Regulation 41.43(a)(6) define ``daily settlement price'' as ``the settlement price of [a] security future determined at the close of trading each day, under the rules of the applicable exchange, clearing agency, or derivatives clearing organization.'' Thus, SEC and CFTC regulations contemplate that exchange rules will determine the applicable settlement price. Under Rule 1215(b), the ``daily settlement price'' would be the ``Daily Settlement Price,'' as determined by Rule 1209 and the relevant Product Appendix. To comply with SEC Rule 242.401(a)(4)(i)(A) and CFTC Regulation 41.43(a)(4)(i)(A), the Exchange intends to regularly publish the Daily Settlement Price. Type, Form and Use of Margin. Rule 1215(c) identifies the types of assets that a security futures intermediary may accept from a Customer as margin. Consistent with SEC Rule 242.404(b) and CFTC Regulation 41.46(b), acceptable assets are limited to: deposits of cash, margin securities (subject to specified restrictions), exempted securities, any other assets permitted under Regulation T of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to satisfy a margin deficiency in a securities margin account, any other assets permitted under CFTC Regulation 41.46 and SEC Rule 242.404, and any combination of the foregoing. Rule 1215(c) further provides that the equity in a Customer account and thus the applicable margin deposit requirements shall be calculated in accordance with CFTC Regulations 41.46(c), 41.46(d), 41.46(e) and 41.46(f) and SEC Rules 242.404(c), 242.404(d), 242.404(e) and 242.404(f), as applicable. The Exchange added the phrase ``any other assets permitted under CFTC Regulation 41.46 and SEC Rule 242.404'' to accommodate other assets that may be permitted under applicable CFTC and SEC regulations in the future. If the SEC, the CFTC or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System amend SEC Rule 242.404, CFTC Regulation 41.46 or Regulation T, respectively, or otherwise provide exemptive or interpretive relief, the Exchange intends to permit Participant Firms and Clearing Firms to collect payment stablecoins as margin. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.270 Clearly Erroneous Executions

1. Purpose In light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 Trading, the Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.270 (``Clearly Erroneous Executions''). Background In conjunction with the industry's plans for the introduction of 23/5 Trading, the Operating Committee of the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility (``LULD Plan'') filed proposed Amendment 27 to the LULD Plan, which proposed to establish price band protections during overnight trading hours (``Overnight Price Bands''). The Operating Committee proposed that the Overnight Price Bands would initially be temporary static bands 20% above and below two reference points, and that after implementation, the Operating Committee would evaluate the performance of such Overnight Price Bands and propose appropriate changes in a new plan amendment. On August 5, 2026, the Commission approved the proposal. In light of the Commission's approval of these changes to the LULD Plan, the Exchange now proposes several amendments to Rule 11.270 regarding Clearly Erroneous Executions. In general, Rule 11.270 describes the process a market participant may use to request cancellation of a transaction that was ``clearly erroneous.'' The current rule's central premise is that if LULD Price Bands under the LULD Plan were available and correct at the time the transaction was executed, the transaction is not eligible for clearly erroneous review. Specifically, Rule 11.270(c)(1) currently provides that ``[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during Regular Market Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous'' except in certain limited circumstances, including when (A) the transaction is in an NMS Stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan (i.e., rights and warrants); (B) the transaction was executed at a time when LULD Price Bands were not available or trading should have been prevented due to a regulatory halt or other halt; or (C) several other limited circumstances. In approving the existing version of the rule, the Commission noted that restricting clearly erroneous review in this way during times when LULD Price Bands were in effect was ``consistent with the Act and will further the goal of providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Price Bands will stand and not be broken . . . . Thus, the proposal is designed to limit the potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review process.'' Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Regular Market Hours, meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Regular Market Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange now proposes to extend the existing restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place. This proposed change would be consistent with the Commission's rationale in approving the current version of the rule because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review in the overnight trading session, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken. Proposed Changes to Rule 11.270(c)(1) To implement this change, the Exchange proposes to add several definitions to Rule 11.270(c)(1). First, the Exchange would add that the term ``LULD Protected Hours'' includes Regular Market Hours and ``Overnight Protected Hours'' defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan. Second, the Exchange would define ``LULD Price Bands'' or ``Price Bands'' to mean the Price Bands defined in Section V of the LULD Plan (i.e., the Price Bands that apply during Regular Market Hours) and ``Overnight Price Bands'' as defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (i.e., the Price Bands that apply to the Overnight Protected Hours from 9:00 p.m. ET through 4:00 a.m. ET). The Exchange proposes to amend the current first sentence of Rule 11.270(c)(1) to replace the phrase ``Regular Market Hours'' with ``LULD Protected Hours,'' to provide that ``[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during LULD Protected Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous . . . .'' This change would extend the LULD-based restrictions on clearly erroneous review currently in place during the Regular Market Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours. The Exchange also proposes to amend Rule 11.270(c)(1)(B)'s reference to ``Percentage Parameter'' to incorporate the Percentage Parameter that applies to Overnight Protected Hours. The amended provision would provide for the applicability of clearly erroneous review if the price of the transaction to buy (sell) that is the subject of the clearly erroneous complaint is greater than (less than) the Reference Price by an amount that equals or exceeds the applicable Percentage Parameter defined in Appendix A to the LULD Plan (with respect to the Price Bands that apply during Regular Market Hours) or the ``Overnight Percentage Parameter'' defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (with respect to Overnight Protected Hours). In addition to these changes, the Exchange also proposes to make a non-substantive change to Rule 11.270(c)(1)(A), substituting the term ``LULD Plan'' for the current text ``the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility Pursuant to Rule 608 of Regulation NMS under the Act (the `Limit Up-Limit Down Plan' or `LULD Plan')'' as the ``LULD Plan'' would be defined in the proposed revision to Rule 11.270(c)(1). Self-Regulatory Organizations; MEMX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Rules To Permit the Listing of Binary Options Overlying Key Performance Indicators

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to adopt rules to permit the listing of binary options overlying key performance indicators (``KPIs'') reported by certain issuers of stock (``binary KPI options'') on MEMX Options. The proposed rules are substantially similar to rules of Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe'') that the Commission recently approved. By way of background, binary options are based on the same framework as traditional, standardized options traded on the Exchange, except the payout of a binary option is a fixed amount contingent upon the occurrence of the option being in- or at-the-money rather than an amount based on the degree to which the option is in-the-money. As a result, payout at expiration of a binary option is an all-or-nothing occurrence. The Exchange does not currently list binary options. The Exchange proposes to adopt rules to permit the listing of binary KPI options. Binary KPI options are European-style, cash-settled options contracts listed on an underlying KPI of an issuer. The exercise settlement value of a binary KPI option is determined not by the market price of the issuer's stock, but by whether a specific financial or operating metric that is reported by the issuer in an earnings-related filing submitted to the Commission meets or exceeds a pre-specified strike level. Summary of Differences From the Cboe Rules The proposed rules are based on, and are substantially similar to, the Cboe Rules, and the Exchange proposes to list binary KPI options on the same issuers and KPIs, with the same contract terms, as the binary KPI options approved for listing on Cboe. Throughout this filing, the Exchange has generally used the same language as the Cboe Proposal where the Exchange is adopting the same approach as Cboe. In addition to non-substantive differences (such as conforming changes to reflect the Exchange's rule numbering, defined terms, and existing rules) and other minor differences described in this filing, the proposed rules differ from the Cboe Rules in the following material respects, each of which is further described below: Rule structure. Cboe adopted its binary KPI option rules in part by amending its existing rules governing binary index options. Because the Exchange does not currently list binary options, the Exchange proposes to adopt the rules applicable to binary KPI options in a single new Chapter 30, to add provisions applicable to binary KPI options to Rules 20.6 (Nullification and Adjustment of Options Transactions including Obvious Errors) and 21.17 (Additional Price Protection Mechanisms and Risk Controls), and to make conforming changes to Rules 16.1 and 16.2 to reflect that the Rules applicable to options trading on the Exchange will include Chapter 30. The proposed rules also make conforming changes to reflect the Exchange's rule numbering, defined terms, and existing rules. Clearing. Cboe intends to clear binary KPI options through Cboe Clear US, LLC (``CCUS''), and the Cboe Proposal describes certain provisions of CCUS's proposed rules. The Exchange proposes to define ``Clearing Corporation,'' for purposes of binary KPI options, as the registered clearing agency designated by the Exchange to clear binary KPI options, and to provide that references in the Rules to The Options Clearing Corporation (``OCC'') mean the Clearing Corporation with respect to binary KPI options. The Exchange will submit a separate proposed rule change to the Commission to designate the registered clearing agency that will serve as the Clearing Corporation for binary KPI options. The Exchange represents that it will not list binary KPI options for trading until the Clearing Corporation is registered with the Commission and operationally ready to clear binary KPI options, all applicable filings and documents of the Clearing Corporation related to binary KPI options are approved by the Commission or effective after review by the Commission, as applicable, the applicable disclosure document required by Rule 9b-1 under the Act is in place, and the other conditions described below are satisfied. Maximum execution price. Proposed Rule 21.17(h) is substantially similar to Cboe Rule 5.34(d), which permits Cboe to designate a maximum execution price for a binary option class, except that, pursuant to proposed Rule 21.17(h), the System will prevent executions of binary KPI options at prices above the Exchange- designated maximum execution price, rather than adjusting such execution prices down to the maximum execution price, as provided in Cboe Rule 5.34(d). Consistent with that rule, the Exchange will designate the maximum execution price for each class of binary KPI options and will notify Options Members of the designated maximum execution price. Opening. Cboe Rule 5.31(d)(1)(D) provides that the opening rotation for binary KPI options is initiated at 9:30 a.m. Proposed Rule 30.6(f) instead provides that binary KPI options will open for trading in accordance with Rule 21.7 (Market Opening Procedures), with the stock of the issuer treated as the security underlying the option for purposes of that Rule. Trading functionality. Binary KPI options will generally be subject to the same trading functionality on MEMX Options as other options listed on the Exchange. The Exchange does not currently offer complex order functionality, auction mechanisms, floor trading, or flexible exchange options (``FLEX'') on MEMX Options, and, accordingly, the discussion in the Cboe Proposal of the application of such functionality to binary KPI options does not apply to the Exchange's proposal. Binary options are based on the same framework as traditional, standardized options traded on the Exchange, except the payout of a binary option is a fixed amount contingent upon the occurrence of the option being in- or at-the-money rather than an amount based on the degree to which the option is in-the-money. As a result, payout at expiration of a binary option is an all-or-nothing occurrence. Similar to the approved proposal by Cboe, the Exchange proposes to amend its Rules to permit the listing of binary KPI options. Binary KPI options are European-style, cash-settled options contracts listed on an underlying KPI of an issuer. The exercise settlement value of a binary KPI option is determined not by the market price of the issuer's stock, but by whether a specific financial or operating metric that is reported by the issuer in an earnings-related filing submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the ``Commission'') meets or exceeds a pre-specified strike level. Similar to the approved proposal by Cboe, the Exchange proposes to adopt Rule 1819 (Binary KPI Options) of the Exchange's Rules to describe binary KPI options. Proposed Exchange Rule 1819(a) (Applicability of Binary KPI Options Rules) would provide that the Rules in proposed Rule 1819 apply only to binary KPI options. All other Rules apply to the trading of binary KPI options, except as otherwise provided or the context otherwise requires. The Exchange also proposes to adopt Rule 1819(b) (Definitions), which is based on Cboe Rule 4.70. Like other standardized options, binary KPI options have standardized terms that are established by the Exchange. Standardized terms for binary KPI options include the exercise criterion that is the condition or criterion of a binary KPI option, the exercise settlement amount (i.e., payout amount), the strike price, the expiration date, the settlement type as A.M.- settlement or P.M.-settlement, the exercise style (as European-style), and the requirements used to determine if the KPI condition or criterion of a binary KPI option has been met (the ``payout determination''). The Exchange proposes to establish these terms and additional provisions in new Rule 1819(a), as described below. The Exchange proposes to define a ``binary KPI option'' in new Rule 1819(b) as a cash-settled option contract listed on an underlying KPI of an issuer with an exercise settlement amount that is established at the creation of the option and with a settlement value that is determined by whether a specific KPI disclosed by the issuer in an earnings-related filing submitted to the Commission meets or exceeds its exercise price. Binary KPI options are paid out if the reported value of the applicable KPI (1) equals or is greater than (as the payout determination requirement) the exercise price for a call binary KPI option or (2) is less than (as the payout determination requirement) the exercise price for a put binary KPI option. The Exchange also proposes to provide that unless the context dictates otherwise, the terms underlying security, equity, or index, or any variations of these terms, in the Rules mean issuer KPI for purposes of binary KPI options. The Exchange proposes to define a ``call binary KPI option'' as an option contract that returns an exercise settlement amount if the settlement value of the underlying KPI is at or above the exercise price at expiration (i.e., in- or at-the-money). The term ``Clearing Corporation'' would mean the registered clearing agency designated by the Exchange to clear binary KPI options. For binary KPI options, the exercise price is the exercise threshold of an option contract that establishes the number, value or measure that is compared against the settlement value of the underlying KPI to determine if the cash payout amount (i.e., the exercise settlement amount) will be paid out. In other words, binary KPI options will have a threshold number as the exercise price that will be used to determine if the exercise criterion of the binary KPI option has been met, in which case the option will be exercised and holders will receive the cash payout amount (i.e., the exercise settlement amount). For binary KPI options, the exercise threshold will be a number that reflects or is compared to the underlying KPI of the binary option. 1. Purpose The proposed rule change is intended to maintain harmony between MSRB Rule G-3(g), on retaking of qualification examinations, and FINRA Rule 1210.06 relating to the minimum required waiting periods between an individual's attempts to take and pass FINRA's professional qualification examinations. The proposed rule change is made in furtherance of promoting greater regulatory consistency and operational efficiency for regulated entities in complying with both FINRA and MSRB rules by maintaining professional qualification standards without reducing protection of investors and the public interest. MSRB Rule G-3 requires persons to be appropriately qualified in the classification category corresponding to their functional role by taking and passing the requisite professional qualification examination. If a person fails an MSRB qualification examination, as aforementioned, MSRB Rule G-3(g) sets forth the time a person must wait before retaking a qualification examination. Currently, for the first and second failed attempts, a person must wait 30 days from the date of the prior examination to retake the qualification examination. After three or more failed attempts within a two-year period, a person must wait 180 calendar days from the date of the prior examination to retake the qualification examination. Background The MSRB adopted the timeframes currently provided by MSRB Rule G- 3(g) in 1978 as part of a suite of proposed rule changes establishing professional qualification standards for municipal securities professionals. In its rule proposal, the MSRB noted that the required waiting periods between examination attempts allow for more than one opportunity to pass an examination, while also establishing certain minimum periods between such attempts to ``encourage better preparation.'' Self-Regulatory Organizations; 24X National Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Limited Liability Agreement of 24X US Holdings LLC in Connection With the Expansion of the Warrant Performance Incentive Program

1. Purpose The Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to amend the Fourth Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement (the ``24X US Holdco LLC Agreement'') of 24X US Holdings LLC (``24X US Holdco'') to include amendments related to the issuance of additional Non-Voting Common Units of 24X US Holdco upon expansion of the Exchange's warrant performance incentive program. The proposed amendments are discussed below. On November 5, 2026, the Exchange filed with the Commission a proposal to revise its warrant performance incentive program (``Program'') by making additional Non-Voting Common Units available to be purchased by Program participants starting in the first quarter of 2027 under different terms than those applicable to the Non-Voting Common Units already available to be purchased through the Program. The Exchange proposes to amend the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement to facilitate the expansion of the Program by authorizing 24X US Holdco to issue additional Non-Voting Common Units. The first sentence of paragraph (a) of Section III of the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement currently states that ``[t]he Company is authorized to issue 12,465,282 Common Units as follows: (1) 11,365,282 Voting Common Units, and (2) 1,100,000 Non-Voting Common Units.'' The Exchange proposes to revise this sentence to increase the total number of Common Units that the Company is authorized to issue from 12,465,282 Common Units to 15,222,425 Common Units, by increasing the total number of Non-Voting Common Units from 1,100,000 Non-Voting Common Units to 3,857,143 Non- Voting Common Units. Accordingly, the first sentence of paragraph (a) of Section III of the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement would read as follows: ``The Company is authorized to issue 15,222,425 Common Units as follows: (1) 11,365,282 Voting Common Units, and (2) 3,857,143 Non- Voting Common Units.'' 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change would further the objectives of Section 6(b)(1) of the Act, in particular, in that such amendments enable the Exchange to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Act and to comply with the provisions of the Act, the rules and regulations thereunder, and the rules of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed amendments to the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement related to the expansion of the Program, including the issuance of additional Non-Voting Common Units, are consistent with the Act. Such proposed changes to the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement would facilitate additional participation in the Program, which would encourage Participants to provide additional volume and liquidity to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that an increase in volume and liquidity would benefit all market participants by providing more trading opportunities and tighter spreads, even to those market participants that do not participate in the Program, thereby perfecting the mechanism for a free and open market and national market system. Furthermore, as described in the Program Expansion Release, the addition of Non-Voting Common Units available for purchase through the expanded Program is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because such Non-Voting Common Units are available to all Program participants on the same terms and conditions. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change regarding the issuance of additional Non-Voting Common Units pursuant to the expansion of the Program would increase both intermarket and intramarket competition by incentivizing Participants to add liquidity to the Exchange, which will enhance the quality of quoting and increase the volume of securities traded on the Exchange. To the extent that there is an additional competitive burden on non-Participants, the Exchange believes that such burden is appropriate because the Program should incentivize Participants to add liquidity to the Exchange and thus enhance the volume of securities traded on the Exchange. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 21.2(a), 21.6(c), and 21.7(b)(1) and (c) for the Queuing Period, Order and Quote Entry, and Opening Auction Times Regarding the Global Trading Hours (“GTH”) Sessions

Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 21.2(a), 21.6(c), and 21.7(b)(1) and (c) for the Queuing Period, Order and Quote Entry, and Opening Auction Times Regarding the Global Trading Hours (“GTH”) Sessions

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rules 21.2(a), 21.6(c), and 21.7(b)(1) and (c) to permit the Queuing Period and order and quote entry on BZX Options to begin earlier than they do today. The proposed rule change is substantively identical to the changes Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe Options'') recently made to the Queuing Period, order and quote entry, and opening auction update dissemination times in Cboe Options Rules 5.7(a), 5.31(b)(1), and 5.31(c) for option classes other than index options eligible for Global Trading Hours (``GTH''). Background BZX Options currently operates a single trading session. The Queuing Period is the time period prior to the initiation of an opening rotation during which the System accepts orders and quotes in the Queuing Book for participation in the opening rotation for the applicable trading session. Under current Rule 21.7(b)(1), the Queuing Period begins at 7:30 a.m. Eastern Time for all classes. Consistent with that time, current Rule 21.2(a) provides that the Exchange will begin accepting orders at 7:30 a.m. Eastern Time, as described in Rule 21.7. Under current Rule 21.7(c), the Exchange disseminates opening auction updates for a series beginning at a time (determined by the Exchange) no earlier than one hour prior to the expected initiation of the opening rotation and until the conclusion of the opening rotation for a series. Pre-Opening Queuing Period Start Time The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 21.7(b)(1) to provide that the Queuing Period for Opening Auctions begins at such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., for all classes. Moving the start of the Queuing Period to no earlier than 6:00 a.m. allows the Exchange to lengthen the pre-opening Queuing Period, affording market participants additional time to enter, modify, and cancel orders and quotes for participation in the opening rotation and promoting a smoother, more orderly opening. This change is administrative and ministerial in nature. It adjusts only the time window during which orders and quotes are accepted for the Queuing Book and does not alter trading mechanics, order priority, execution logic, or price formation. Participants are not required to submit orders earlier; the extended window simply provides additional flexibility for those who choose to use it. This change affects only when orders and quotes are accepted for the Queuing Book, not when trading begins; the opening rotation times remain unchanged. The Exchange's approach provides for a start time determined by Exchange notice rather than a fixed time, affording the Exchange operational flexibility. For consistency, the Exchange also proposes to amend the opening auction update dissemination time in Rule 21.7(c) to begin at such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., so that the Exchange may begin disseminating opening auction updates at the start of the Queuing Period (and thus incorporate orders and quotes submitted during the entire Queuing Period in those updates). The Exchange also proposes to amend Rules 21.2(a) and 21.6(c) to update the order and quote entry times to conform to the proposed Queuing Period change in Rule 21.7(b)(1). As amended, Rule 21.2(a) will provide that the Exchange will begin accepting orders at such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m., as described in Rule 21.7, and Rule 21.6(c) will provide that orders can be entered into the System (or previously entered orders cancelled) from such time as the Exchange determines, but no earlier than 6:00 a.m. Eastern Time, until market close. These changes ensure that Users can begin entering orders and quotes at the same time the System begins accepting orders and quotes into the Queuing Book. Because Rule 21.18(c)(1) provides that the System accepts complex orders for inclusion in the COB Opening Process at the times and in the manner set forth in Rule 21.7, the proposed change to the Queuing Period start time will also apply to the entry of complex orders for the COB Opening Process. These changes are administrative in nature. The Queuing Period concept already exists, and the opening auction update dissemination process is unchanged in substance. The change raises no novel policy questions. It merely expands an existing administrative preparation window without affecting how orders are prioritized, matched, or executed. The Exchange notes that while NYSE American LLC's (``NYSE American'') extended trading hours framework provides for a fixed 6:00 a.m. order acceptance time rather than a time determined by Exchange notice, the Exchange believes its discretionary approach is appropriate. The rule merely sets a floor (``no earlier than 6:00 a.m.''); it does not mandate the Exchange to begin queuing at that time. All Exchange determinations regarding the time at which the Queuing Period will begin will be announced via Exchange Notice, so market participants will have advance notice and transparency regarding the applicable start time. In addition, the Exchange believes providing the Exchange with discretion affords operational flexibility to adjust the start time in response to feedback from market participants and evolving market conditions, which benefits investors by allowing the Exchange to optimize the preparation window based on actual market participant needs. The proposed rule change does not amend the operation of the Queuing Period following a trading halt pursuant to Rule 21.7(g), and does not change any other aspect of the opening auction process. Self-Regulatory Organizations; 24X National Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing of a Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Rules To Govern the Trading of Options on the Exchange

1. Purpose The Exchange is proposing to adopt a series of rules in connection with the trading of options, including rules to permit the listing of binary options overlying key performance indicators (``KPIs'') reported by certain issuers of stock (``binary KPI options''), on 24X Options, which will be a facility of the Exchange. 24X Options will operate an electronic trading system developed to trade options (the ``System''). The Exchange will operate its options market much as it operates its cash equities market today and in a manner similar to that of other options exchanges, with a comprehensive suite of conventional order types and functionality that is designed to provide for an efficient, robust, and transparent order matching process. The proposed functionality for 24X Options is substantially similar to that offered by other options exchanges. Thus, the Exchange proposes to adopt rules applicable to 24X Options that are substantively identical or substantially similar to the approved options rules of MEMX, except for the rules related to binary KPI options which are substantively identical or substantially similar to the approved rules of Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe'') for binary KPI options. The System will provide for the electronic display and execution of orders in price/time priority without regard to the status of the entities that are entering orders. All Exchange Members will be eligible to participate in 24X Options provided that the Exchange specifically authorizes them to trade in the System. The System will provide a routing service via unaffiliated routing broker-dealers for orders when trading interest is not present on 24X Options and will comply with all applicable securities laws and regulations and the obligations of the Options Order Protection and Locked/Crossed Market Plan. 24X Options Members Pursuant to the proposed rules in Chapter 17 (Participation on 24X Options), the Exchange will authorize any Exchange Member that meets certain enumerated qualification requirements (any such Member, an ``Options Member'') and any Options Member's Sponsored Participants to obtain access to, and transact business on, 24X Options. There will be two types of Options Members--Options Order Entry Firms (``OEFs'') and Options Market Makers. OEFs will be those Options Members representing Customer Orders as agent on 24X Options or trading as principal on 24X Options. Options Market Makers will be those Options Members registered with the Exchange as Options Market Makers pursuant to proposed Rule 22.2. To become an Options Market Maker, an Options Member will be required to register by filing a written application. The Exchange will not place any limit on the number of entities that may become Options Market Makers, the number of appointments an Options Market Maker may have, or the number of Options Market Makers that may have appointments in a class unless the Exchange determines to impose any such limit based on system constraints, capacity restrictions, or other factors relevant to protecting the integrity of the System. The Exchange will not impose any such limitations until it has submitted objective standards for imposing the limits to the Commission for its review and approval. As set forth in proposed Rule 22.6, Options Market Makers will be required to electronically engage in a course of dealing reasonably calculated to contribute to the maintenance of fair and orderly markets. Among other things, an Options Market Maker would generally have to satisfy the following responsibilities and duties during trading: (1) on a daily basis maintain a two-sided market on a continuous basis in at least 60% of the cumulative number of seconds, or such higher percentage as the Exchange may announce in advance, for which that Options Market Maker's appointed classes are open for trading, excluding any adjusted series, any intraday add-on series on the day during which such series are added for trading, any Quarterly Option Series, and any series with an expiration of greater than 270 days; (2) enter a size of at least one contract for its best bid and its best offer; and (3) maintain minimum net capital in accordance with Commission and Exchange rules. Substantial or continued failure by an Options Market Maker to meet any of its obligations and duties will subject the Options Market Maker to disciplinary action, suspension, or revocation of the Options Market Maker's registration as such or its appointment in one or more of its appointed options classes. The quoting obligations of Options Market Makers set forth in proposed Rule 22.6 are substantively identical to MEMX Rule 22.6. Options Market Makers would also be required to (1) identify all accounts related to their market making activities to the Exchange; (2) report to the Exchange upon request all orders in securities underlying options traded on the Exchange or securities convertible into or exchangeable for such underlying security; and (3) comply with certain joint account restrictions. The foregoing requirements are set forth in proposed Rule 22.7, which is substantively identical to MEMX Rule 22.7. Options Market Makers receive certain benefits for carrying out their duties. For example, a lender may extend credit to a broker- dealer without regard to the restrictions in Regulation T of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System if the credit is to be used to finance the broker-dealer's activities as a specialist or market maker on a national securities exchange. Thus, an Options Market Maker has a corresponding obligation to hold itself out as willing to buy and sell options for its own account on a regular or continuous basis to justify this favorable treatment. Every Options Member shall at all times maintain membership in another registered options exchange that is not registered solely under Section 6(g) of the Exchange Act or in FINRA. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Reduce the Clearing Fee for Securities Contracts

1. Purpose CCUS proposes to amend its Fee Schedule, effective November 13, 2026, to assess no clearing fees on Securities Contracts by reducing the Clearing Member Clearing Fee and the Clearing Member Position Transfer Fee for Securities Contracts from $0.0001 per cleared contract to $0.0000 per cleared contract. The reduced fees will apply equally to all Securities Contract transactions. CCUS is proposing to reduce its clearing fees for Securities Contracts in connection with the launch of clearing of Binary KPI Options on CCUS to encourage market participants to trade Binary KPI Options. CCUS's participating exchange for Securities Contracts, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe Options'' or the ``Exchange''), has separately filed a proposed rule change to waive fees associated with the trading of Binary KPI Options in connection with its launch of the new product. CCUS believes that the reduction in Securities Contract clearing fees from $0.0001 to $0.0000 complements the Exchange's waiver of fees related to Binary KPI Options and will further encourage clearing firms to support, and market participants to trade, the new product. This approach is consistent with practice at other registered clearing agencies, which have waived clearing-related fees to encourage participation in new clearing services or products. The Clearinghouse may revisit the clearing fees applicable to Securities Contracts in the future, and any such change would be the subject of a separate rule filing. 2. Statutory Basis CCUS believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a registered clearing agency. In particular, CCUS believes that the proposed reduction in clearing fees for Securities Contracts provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable fees among its participants, consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(D) of the Act. CCUS believes that reducing its clearing fees to $0.0000 for Securities Contracts is reasonable because it assesses no clearing fee for Securities Contracts in any capacity, and thus no market participant will pay more as a result of the proposed rule change. CCUS further believes the proposed reduction of the clearing fee for Securities Contracts from $0.0001 to $0.0000 per cleared contract is reasonable because it complements the waiver of transaction fees for Binary KPI Options adopted by Cboe Options, further lowering the total cost of trading Binary KPI Options for all Clearing Members. More generally, CCUS believes it is reasonable to assess no fees in connection with the launch of a new product because doing so is designed to encourage participation in Binary KPI Options and thereby promote liquid and active markets in these Securities Contracts, to the benefit of all market participants. CCUS notes that fee reductions and waivers in connection with the launch of new products are a common practice among clearing agencies and exchanges, and that the Commission has previously permitted such fee changes to become effective upon filing. CCUS further notes that the fee reduction is designed to apply during the initial launch period, and CCUS will evaluate the fee level for Securities Contracts as the market for Binary KPI Options develops; any future change to the fee will be subject to a rule filing with the Commission. CCUS also believes that the proposed fee reduction is reasonable and has been set at an appropriate level given the costs, expenses, and revenues associated with providing clearing services for Securities Contracts, because CCUS has determined that it can forgo the revenue from the decrease in fees and continue to cover its operating expenses and regulatory financial resource requirements. The fee reduction will not affect CCUS's risk management practices, margin methodology, or the resources available to CCUS to manage the default of a Clearing Member, and CCUS will continue to maintain financial resources in accordance with applicable Commission rules. Finally, CCUS also believes the reduced clearing fee is equitably allocated because it will apply uniformly to all transactions in Securities Contracts and all Clearing Members, each of which will have the same opportunity to benefit from the reduction. CCUS also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act, which requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions. Eliminating clearing costs for Securities Contracts in connection with the launch of Binary KPI Options clearing at CCUS will lower the cost of accessing CCUS clearing services. CCUS believes this will encourage Clearing Members to clear these products at CCUS and will promote clearing activity in them. By facilitating access to CCUS's clearance and settlement services in this way, the proposed rule change will thereby promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of transactions in these products. CCUS also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 17A(b)(3)(F) requirement that the rules of a clearing agency not be designed to permit unfair discrimination in the admission of participants or among participants in the use of the clearing agency because, as discussed above, the reduced clearing fee will apply equally to all transactions. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend FINRA Rules 6380A and 6380B (Transaction Reporting) To Extend the Limited, Temporary Exception From Reporting Specified Overnight Transactions Prior to 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time Until December 31, 2027
