Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend FINRA Rules 6380A and 6380B (Transaction Reporting) To Extend the Limited, Temporary Exception From Reporting Specified Overnight Transactions Prior to 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time Until December 31, 2027

1. Purpose Background The TRFs are facilities of FINRA that are operated by NYSE Market (DE), Inc. (in the case of the FINRA/NYSE TRF) and Nasdaq, Inc. (in the case of the FINRA/Nasdaq TRF Carteret and the FINRA/Nasdaq TRF Chicago). Along with the Alternative Display Facility (``ADF''), the TRFs provide FINRA members with a mechanism for the reporting of over- the-counter (``OTC'') trades in NMS stocks. While members are required to report all OTC trades in NMS stocks to FINRA, they may choose which FINRA facility (or facilities) to use to satisfy their trade reporting obligations. All trade reports submitted to the TRFs, other than non- tape reports, are reported to and publicly disseminated by the appropriate SIP. In March 2026, FINRA extended the opening time of the TRFs from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m., such that the current operating hours of the TRFs are 4:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. each business day. These operating hours are reflected in the transaction reporting rules for the FINRA/ Nasdaq TRFs (FINRA Rule 6380A (Transaction Reporting)) and the FINRA/ NYSE TRF (FINRA Rule 6380B (Transaction Reporting)). In July 2026, FINRA adopted amendments to Rules 6320A, 6320B, 6380A and 6380B to further extend the TRF hours such that the TRFs will be operational from 9:00 p.m. on Sundays to 8:00 p.m. Fridays, excluding holidays, with a one-hour pause from 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Monday through Thursday, thereby enabling real-time public dissemination through the SIPs of trade reports for OTC transactions in NMS stocks 23 hours per day, five days per week. The TRF 23/5 Amendments are scheduled to be implemented on December 6, 2026. In connection with the TRF Early Open Amendments, FINRA provided a limited, temporary exception under Supplementary Material .05 to Rules 6380A and 6380B to permit qualifying overnight transactions to continue to be reported by 8:15 a.m. Specifically, Supplementary Material .05(a)(1) provides that last sale reports for qualifying overnight transactions executed between midnight and 8:00 a.m. may be reported by 8:15 a.m. on trade date and be designated with the unique trade report modifier, as specified by FINRA, to denote their execution outside normal market hours. Supplementary Material .05(a)(2) provides that last sale reports for qualifying overnight transactions executed (i) between 8:00 p.m. and midnight or (ii) on any non-business day (i.e., weekend or holiday) may be reported the following business day by 8:15 a.m., be designated ``as/of'' trades to denote their execution on a prior day and be designated with the unique trade report modifier, as specified by FINRA, to denote their execution outside normal market hours. Collectively, these provisions of Supplementary Material .05 allow members to continue to report qualifying overnight transactions on the same timeframes as generally applied prior to the TRF Early Open Amendments. Under Supplementary Material .05, this temporary exception is in effect until the earlier of (i) the effective date of any amendments to further extend the TRF operating hours or (ii) December 31, 2027. Thus, absent further action, the temporary exception for qualifying overnight transactions will by its terms expire on December 6, 2026, when the TRFs expand their hours pursuant to the TRF 23/5 Amendments. In response to member concerns regarding the need for more time to address operational challenges associated with reporting specified overnight transactions, FINRA is now proposing to extend the limited, temporary exception for reporting qualifying overnight transactions until December 31, 2027, as described in greater detail below. Proposed Extension of Exception for Specified Overnight Transactions FINRA is proposing to amend Supplementary Material .05(c) to Rules 6380A and 6380B to extend the availability of the trade reporting exception until December 31, 2027, generally permitting members to continue to report qualifying overnight transactions by 8:15 a.m. Specifically, the proposed rule change would remove the current reference to the exception being in effect until the earlier of the effective date of any extension of TRF operating hours and December 31, 2027, and instead provide that the exception is in effect until December 31, 2027. The proposed rule change would thus provide just over one additional year for members to adapt their processes to accommodate real-time overnight and early morning reporting for qualifying overnight transactions. FINRA believes this extension would provide sufficient time for members to address operational challenges while still providing an outer effective date for members to begin reporting such transactions in real time. While the proposed rule change would not alter the substance of the existing relief under paragraph (a) of Supplementary Material .05 (or the definition of ``qualifying overnight transaction'' under paragraph (b) of Supplementary Material .05), it would make several conforming and clarifying changes to these provisions to account for the new defined terms used in Rules 6380A and 6380B as amended by the TRF 23/5 Amendments. First, the proposed rule change would replace the term ``normal market hours'' with the new defined term ``Regular Trading Hours'' in paragraphs (a) and (b) of Supplementary Material .05. Second, the proposed rule change would replace the term ``business day'' with the new defined term ``Business Day'' in paragraph (a) of Supplementary Material .05. Finally, the proposed rule change would amend paragraph (a) of Supplementary Material .05 to account for the new definition of ``Trade Date'' under the TRF 23/5 Amendments. Specifically, paragraph (a)(1) would be amended to provide that last sale reports executed between 8:00 p.m. on a Calendar Day preceding a Business Day and 8:00 a.m. on a Business Day may be reported by 8:15 a.m. on such Business Day and be designated with the unique trade report modifier, as specified by FINRA, to denote their execution outside R

[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 224 (Monday, November 23, 2026)] [Notices] [Pages 75574-75580] From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov] [FR Doc No: 2026-23743] ======================================================================= ----------------------------------------------------------------------- SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION [Release No. 34-106927; File No. SR-DTC-2026-012] Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Depository Trust Company; Notice of Filing of Partial Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, To Modernize the Direct Registration System November 18, 2026. On September 29, 2026, the Depository Trust Company (``DTC'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'') proposed rule change SR-DTC-2026-012, pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder. The proposed rule change would amend the Deposits Guide and the Fee Guide in connection with DTC's modernization of its Direct Registration Service (``DRS''). The proposed rule change was published for comment in the Federal Register on October 5, 2026. The Commission has received comments regarding the substance of the changes proposed in the proposed rule change. On November 6, 2026, DTC filed Partial Amendment No. 1 to the proposed rule change to postpone the implementation date of the proposed rule change until no later than June 30, 2027, with specific implementation date announced by Important Notice at least 14 days in advance. Partial Amendment No. 1 does not substantively change the proposed rule change. The proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, is hereinafter referred to as the ``Proposed Rule Change.'' The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on Partial Amendment No. 1 from interested persons, and for the reasons discussed below, the Commission is approving the Proposed Rule Change, on an accelerated basis. I. Background DTC serves as a central securities depository and operates a securities settlement system. DTC's activities include holding securities in physical or dematerialized form, maintaining securities accounts for Participants, providing central safekeeping and asset services, transfers and pledges of securities, and settling transactions by book entry (free of payment or delivery-versus- payment), as well as processing instructions for corporate action offers, elections, solicitations, or tabulations. DRS is a DTC service that allows investors to hold DRS-eligible securities (``DRS Securities'') in two ways. Investors may hold them indirectly through DTC's book-entry holding model, commonly called holding in ``street name.'' Alternatively, they may hold them directly on the books of the issuer's transfer agent, if that transfer agent is a DTC DRS Agent (``DRS Agent''), commonly called direct registration. DRS allows investors to move DRS Securities between the two holding structures without the issuance of a paper certificate. DRS transfers are processed through three types of instructions: DRS Profile Deposit Requests, DRS Deliver Orders, and DRS Withdrawal by Transfer instructions. DRS Profile Deposit Requests. A DRS Profile Deposit Request is used to move DRS Securities from an investor's account at a DRS Agent, where the shares are registered in the investor's name, to a Participant's account at DTC, where the shares are registered in the name of DTC's nominee, Cede & Co. (``Cede''), i.e., to move from direct registration to holding in street name. To initiate the transfer, the Participant must submit a DRS Profile Deposit Request to DTC, which the DRS Agent must then approve. Upon the DRS Agent's approval, the shares are re-registered to Cede and moved from the DRS Agent to DTC, which credits the shares to the Participant's account. If the DRS Agent rejects the request, the transaction status is updated with the reason for the rejection, and the Participant is notified. DRS Profile Deposits must be covered by Profile Surety in order to be processed by DTC. DRS Deliver Orders. Alternatively, an investor may transfer DRS Securities to its account with a Participant by instructing the DRS Agent directly. The DRS Agent then creates a DRS Deliver Order without a DRS Profile Deposit Request, which is completed through DTC's standard Deliver Order process. The receiving Participant is not required to approve or accept the DRS Deliver Order but may reject it after receipt. DRS Withdrawal by Transfer. A DRS Withdrawal by Transfer instruction, which can only be initiated by the Participant, moves shares in the opposite direction, i.e., from holding in street name to direct registration. An investor seeking to move shares out of Cede's name and into the investor's account at the DRS Agent must therefore request the withdrawal through its Participant. The Participant then submits the instruction, requesting that the shares be removed from their free position at DTC and credited, in the investor's name, to the investor's account at the DRS Agent. If the DRS Agent approves the request, the shares are moved out of Cede's name and into the investor's name and credited to the investor's DRS account on the DRS Agent's books. If the DRS Agent rejects the request, the Participant is notified, and the transaction status is updated with the reason for the rejection. Currently, Participants and DRS Agents submit, review, approve, and complete DRS transfers through multiple steps and manual operational processes. They also rely on a combination of legacy applications, including the Participant Terminal System (``PTS'') and the Participant Browser Service (``PBS'') functions, as well as CCF batch-file processing. Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Relating to Operational Rule Changes

[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 224 (Monday, November 23, 2026)] [Notices] [Pages 75614-75626] From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov] [FR Doc No: 2026-23742] ----------------------------------------------------------------------- SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION [Release No. 34-106926; File No. SR-CMESC-2026-009] Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Relating to Operational Rule Changes November 18, 2026. Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the ``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, notice is hereby given that on November 6, 2026, CME Securities Clearing Inc. (``CMESC'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``SEC'' or ``Commission'') the proposed rule change described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been substantially prepared by CMESC. CMESC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons. I. CMESC's Statement of the Terms and Substance of the Proposed Rule Change The proposed rule change of CME Securities Clearing Inc. (``CMESC'') consists of amendments to the CMESC Rules 101 (Definitions), 503 (Haircut Collateral), 601 (Accounts), 604 (Designation of Banks for Settling Transactions), 1503 (Novation of Transactions), 1504 (Settlement Obligations for Transactions), 1505 (Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Eligible Securities Transactions; Reports), and 1506 (Eligible Securities Transaction Fails). Each of the proposed changes is described in more detail below. II. CMESC's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for the Proposed Rule Change In its filing with the Commission, CMESC included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. CMESC has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements. A. CMESC's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for the Proposed Rule Change (a) Purpose The purpose of the proposed rule change is to (i) clarify the treatment of Haircut Collateral in Clear to Hold Transactions, (ii) modify the Rules regarding accounts and banks that Participants may use to settle deliverable obligations in Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, (iii) modify the description of CMESC's daily settlement reports, including the content of such reports, to reflect CMESC's netting practice with respect to settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions, (iv) clarify and update the descriptions of the settlement obligations and processing in existing Rules to more align with CMESC's settlement practices with respect to Eligible Securities Transactions, (v) update the descriptions of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculations and processes for Eligible Securities Transactions, (vi) update settlement fails provisions, and (vii) make certain other technical, administrative, clarifying and conforming changes to ensure consistency and improve clarity and readability of the Rules. Specifically, CMESC proposes to: 1. Amend Rules 503(b) and 101 to better describe certain features of Haircut Collateral in Clear to Hold Transactions; 2. Amend Rules 601, 604, 1504(c) and 101 to provide Participants with a wider range of options for banks used to settle securities delivery obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; 3. Amend Rules 1504(e) and 101 regarding CMESC's daily settlement reports, including updated descriptions to reflect CMESC's practice with respect to netting settlement obligations for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; 4. Amend Rules 1504(d), (f) and (g) to consolidate duplicative text and revise the descriptions of settlement and netting procedures for Clear to Deliver Transactions, Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Hold Transactions for greater consistency, while also amending Rule 1504(f) to permit CMESC to settle obligations resulting from a same-day settling Cash Treasury Transaction or Clear to Deliver Transaction directly with the Participant counterparties to a riskless principal, without delivering securities or making payment to the riskless principal, where the riskless principal and its Participant counterparties have identical and offsetting settlement obligations, and amending Rule 1504(f)(v) to clarify certain operational timelines; 5. Amend Rule 1505 to update the description of CMESC's calculation and processing of Outstanding Exposure Settlement for Eligible Securities Transactions, including: a. Amending Rules 1505(a) and 1505(d) to update the description of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculation and process for Clear to Hold Transactions; b. Amending Rules 1505(b), 1505(c) and 1505(f) to update the description of Outstanding Exposure Settlement calculation and processing for Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; and c. Amending Rule 1505(b)(ii) to address processing for atypical trades such as transfers and related cash adjustments; 6. Amend Rule 1506 to update partial settlement fails provisions for both Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions and for Clear to Hold Transactions, including amending Rule 1506(h) to restrict CMESC's buy-in rights only to Cash Treasury Transactions and Clear to Deliver Transactions; and 7. Make certain other technical, administrative, clarifying and conforming changes to ensure consistency and improve clarity and readability of the Rules.
